Back in the Void Secret Realm, the Elder of the Long Sword killed my Third and Fifth Martial Uncles. My Chongyang Mountain shares an irreconcilable hatred with him, and we are determined to use his blood to sacrifice to our departed."

Hongfu scanned the young Taoist up and down and said, "You are young, yet your cultivation is quite good; you are a standout among the younger generation. It is thoughtful of Chongyang Mountain to send you. You may follow me these days. Once we find that old man of the Long Sword, I will let you take his head back to report."

Yue Qingfeng bowed in thanks and added, "Martial Aunt, this disciple has discovered that someone is using humans to refine demonic beasts. I fear there are demonic cultivators in this town."

Hongfu rested her head on one hand, closed her eyes to feign sleep, and said dismissively, "Mere demonic cultivators, hiding their heads and showing their tails—they are nothing but clowns, not worth fearing."

Hearing this, Yue Qingfeng said no more and withdrew from the room with the two maids.

Hongfu kept her eyes closed, her mind wandering, and she could not help but recall that day two hundred years ago.

The Void Secret Realm only opened when there was sufficient fortune in the world. It was filled with countless treasures; even the most ordinary flower or grass obtained from within could be refined into an elixir to prolong life.

Thus, the opening of the Void Secret Realm also symbolized the beginning of a slaughterhouse.

Hongfu was one of the few powerhouses, and naturally, she was besieged by those who were still alive. Her strength was transcendent, and she did not take these people seriously. She fought her way to the depths of the secret realm, and seeing a protective formation activate in a cave, she anticipated that there must be peerless treasures inside.

It was then that her martial uncle, the Elder of the Long Sword, appeared.

Hongfu had not expected the sneak attack from the Elder of the Long Sword. She was severely wounded, and just as she was about to fall off a cliff, a man in green grabbed her hand in time, saving her life.

Hongfu was proud and arrogant; she had never needed anyone to save her life.

She only remembered that the man’s face was plain and unremarkable, with no memorable features, but when she was pulled close by him, a breeze blew, and she met the man’s pair of black eyes.

It was precisely because of this glance that she inexplicably remembered him.

He joined forces with her to fight the old man of the Long Sword until he fled on his sword. When Hongfu, heavily injured, could no longer stand and was about to collapse to the ground, the man supported her again.

This man was different from others. Hongfu felt no desire from him; he was not a servant at her feet, which only made her feelings more subtle.

"What is your name? You helped me; whether it is magic treasures, secret manuals, or spiritual elixirs, I can use them as a reward."

The man did not speak.

Hongfu felt a flicker of anger.

In the blink of an eye, the man grabbed her arm and threw her into the protective formation.

Before Hongfu could react, the man had used her as a meat shield against the formation's attack and slipped into the cave like a wisp of smoke.

That day, Hongfu was covered in wounds and had to sacrifice a hundred years of her cultivation using a secret technique to save her own life.

Hongfu’s hand clenched tighter and tighter. Finally, she opened her blood-red eyes, shattered the fine wooden table, and with a murderous aura rising in her eyes, she gritted her teeth.

"No matter if it's the ends of the earth, I will kill you!"

The young man suddenly coughed, breaking the quiet atmosphere.

Mu Ran was squatting in the courtyard, boredly teasing a small crucian carp kept in a water vat with a twig she had picked up. Hearing the movement, she turned her head. "Jinzhi, are you sick?"

Cang Shubai finished hanging up the clean clothes. "I'm fine."

Mu Ran had already darted over, standing on tiptoe to touch his forehead. Feeling no heat, she quickly took out a handkerchief to wipe Cang Shubai’s still-damp hands, muttering to herself with her head lowered.

"Don't go into the water to work these days; I'll do the housework."

"You can't go into the water these days either."

"Why can't I go into the water?"

Cang Shubai said, "It's almost time for your period."

Mu Ran was stunned. "Is it that soon? I forgot."

Cang Shubai poked her forehead with his finger. "No drinking cold water these days, lest you start crying about the pain again."

Mu Ran said "Oh," feeling a bit embarrassed.

Compared to herself, he was the one who truly knew her body inside out.

chapters.title: Workplace Principles
chapters.content:
Cang Shubai remembered correctly; Mu Ran started her period the next day.

She lay limp on the bed, curled up in the quilt, looking sickly and unwilling to get up.

Cang Shubai sat by the bedside, his large hand resting on her lower abdomen, continuously radiating a warm temperature that made Mu Ran feel very comfortable.

She hugged his arm, blinking her eyes obediently. "Jinzhi, I’m fine. You should go to the medical clinic for work."

Although she said that, the way she clung to his arm clearly showed she didn't want him to leave.

Cang Shubai said, "It doesn't matter if I miss a day of work."

Mu Ran shook her head. "No, no. It’s not easy to find work these days. You can't leave a bad impression on your boss, or what if he makes things difficult for you? Jinzhi, you need to learn more about workplace principles."

Cang Shubai had long been accustomed to the strange and curious vocabulary she would occasionally spout. He leaned down, pressing his forehead against hers, quietly feeling her body temperature.

The gesture, which originally held no amorous intent, caused his gaze to flicker when he saw the familiar love and awe for him in the girl’s dark, glistening eyes. Taking advantage of their proximity, he kissed the corner of her lips.

"Ranran, your body is still a bit hot."

Suddenly, the bleeding became heavy. Mu Ran curled up further and pushed him away with both hands. "Jinzhi, when I'm like this, can you stay a little further away from me?"

The scent of blood on her had grown stronger.

The young man’s large hand, still resting on her lower abdomen, slid down slightly. "It was just a kiss; why did you react to it?"

Mu Ran’s face turned beet red. She pushed his hand away and buried her face in the quilt.

She was just a bit more sensitive at this time; what was wrong with being easily affected by him?

They were, after all, a legitimate married couple.

Faintly, she seemed to hear a soft chuckle from him.

Cang Shubai knew she was uncomfortable at times like this and ultimately didn't dare to tease her too much. After all, if she felt unwell or unhappy, he would be the one to feel heartache and have to rack his brains to coax her back to good spirits.

Not long after, a warm hot water bottle was tucked into the quilt. She held it against her stomach and felt the spirit stone embedded in it for continuous warmth, feeling a pang of heartache over the cost.

She often felt that her husband, who came from an unremarkable background, was sometimes even more extravagant than she was when it came to spending money.

"Alright, alright, I'm fine now. Jinzhi, go to work."

Cang Shubai asked, "Are you really okay?"

Mu Ran insisted repeatedly, "Absolutely fine."

Cang Shubai sat quietly for a long time, until a hand slowly reached out from the quilt and grasped his large hand.

He lowered his eyes, cooperatively allowing her fingers to interlace with his.

The girl’s voice was muffled. "Jinzhi, I don't want to be a burden to you."

"You are not a burden to me."

"Then go to work. I can take care of myself. Before I married you, I lived alone just fine."

Cang Shubai gently stroked her fingers, and finally, he compromised. "What do you want to eat?"

"Mung bean cake."

Cang Shubai said, "That’s what I like to eat."

"Whatever Jinzhi likes to eat, I like to eat too."

After a moment of silence, a corner of the quilt was lifted, and most of her face was exposed.

Mu Ran stared blankly at the young man leaning in. Just as he was about to kiss her, he stopped.

Cang Shubai gazed at her with his dark eyes for a long time, one hand gently caressing her cheek. "We’ll continue after your period is over."

Mu Ran: "..."

The next moment, she dove back into the quilt.

Cang Shubai tucked the quilt around her and patted her body gently through the fabric. "Wait for me to come back."

As soon as he left, Mu Ran immediately popped her head out from the quilt. The flush on her face had faded quite a bit, but when she looked up and saw the clean menstrual pads already laid out nearby, her face began to heat up again.

Sometimes, he didn't have to be so attentive.

Butcher Fan was the only butcher in the village who sold meat. Although he had an ambiguous relationship with the widow Li, he had never been lazy when it came to business. However, he had been slacking off lately. Villagers often saw him wandering around, yet he had become increasingly lavish with his spending, telling everyone he met that he had struck it rich.

When others asked him how he had made his fortune, he would act mysterious and stop talking.

On this day, he was wandering around the village idly again, stopping in front of a courtyard gate, unable to resist standing on tiptoe to peek inside.

Auntie Wang shouted from next door, "Fan the Scab, what are you looking at here?"

Butcher Fan cleared his throat and lied through his teeth, "The young doctor bought meat from me a while ago and gave me too much money. I couldn't make change then, but now that I have small change, I wanted to return the extra money to him."

"Then come back another day. The young doctor has gone out; he’s not home right now."

Cang Shubai went to the town's medical clinic almost every day. He knew, of course, that Cang Shubai wasn't home, which was why he hoped to catch a few more glimpses of the beautiful young woman.

But with Auntie Wang watching like a tiger, Butcher Fan had no choice but to give up, hunching his back and walking away unwillingly.

Butcher Fan returned home in a foul mood. Once he closed the door, a fawning smile immediately appeared on his face. "Immortal Elder, I’m back."

An old man with a white beard sat cross-legged on the couch, dressed in white, looking like an immortal.

He opened his eyes; they were clear and deep, bright as cold stars. His brows were sparse and elegant, his long eyebrows drooping to his temples, and his complexion was pure. Though he sat still, he possessed an otherworldly, detached aura, as if he were untainted by the mortal world. One look was enough to know he was an outsider who had practiced for many years with a heart as calm as an abyss.

The old man smiled. "Little friend, what news have you brought back today?"

Butcher Fan said, "Many cultivators have come to town. Among them is one called Fairy Hongfu. She is as beautiful as the Fairy Hongling in the stories! Many people want to catch a glimpse of her face to see if she is truly as stunning as the rumors say!"

Butcher Fan smacked his lips. "I haven't seen Fairy Hongfu, but I think when it comes to being stunning, Cang Shubai’s wife is definitely one of them. That little face, that slender waist—she’s incredibly alluring when she walks. And that voice, it’s as sweet as an oriole’s. It’s a pity I can’t even touch her hand."

The old man seemed not to notice the greed in Butcher Fan’s eyes and said kindly, "You want to touch the lady's hand?"

Butcher Fan wanted much more than just to touch her hand, but he didn't dare reveal too much desire in front of the Immortal Elder. He hurriedly said, "That’s not what I meant; I was just lamenting how lucky Cang Shubai is."

"Everyone has an appreciation for beauty, and people have seven emotions and six desires; that is perfectly normal." The old man took out a medicine bottle and several spirit stones. "You and I are fated, little friend. I will help you achieve your heart's desire, and you will help me do one thing. How about that?"

Butcher Fan was dazzled by the spirit stones. He hurriedly took them, beaming with joy, and asked, "What does the Immortal Elder want me to do? Just say it!"

"At midnight, sprinkle the powder in this bottle into the village well."

Butcher Fan was stunned. "This..."

The Immortal Elder smiled. "Don't worry. The bottle contains a spiritual medicine that can help this small place develop a spiritual vein. Once there is a spiritual vein, the villagers will benefit too. For me, this is an act of merit that will also help increase my cultivation. It’s a win-win situation; why wouldn't you do it, little friend? Besides, I was seriously injured, and you saved me and brought me home. How could I return kindness with evil?"

Butcher Fan touched the spirit stones in his hand, a smile appearing on his face again, and he nodded impatiently. "Alright, I’ll listen to the Immortal Elder."

chapters.title: The Little Wooden Figure
chapters.content:
Every time Mu Ran had her period, she would only feel a heavy, dragging sensation in her lower abdomen during the first two days, though it didn't quite qualify as pain.

This discomfort was usually something she could endure. After all, most women had even more intense reactions during their periods, yet they still went about their work as usual and didn't treat such discomfort as anything worth noting.

When Mu Ran lived alone in the past, she never felt this discomfort was unbearable. It was only after marrying Cang Shubai that she seemed to have become increasingly delicate.

Although Cang Shubai had gone to work at the town’s medical clinic at Mu Ran’s strong insistence, he returned earlier than usual again today, citing the same reason: there weren't many patients at the clinic.

Cang Shubai placed the still-warm mung bean cakes on the table. Catching sight of Mu Ran tinkering with her pile of wooden parts again, he sat down beside her and, without a word, took her hand in his.

Mu Ran had no choice but to pause her handiwork.

Cang Shubai had always been considerate and gentle with her, but sometimes, she would vaguely feel that he was actually a very forceful person. For instance, there were times when he would grab her hand regardless of her wishes, and she would be unable to pull it away.

He said, "Your hands are a bit cold."

Mu Ran blinked. "Are they? I don't feel it."

He would sometimes say her body was hot, other times that it was cold, as if he had absolute knowledge of her body temperature. Once it fluctuated above or below the normal range, he felt compelled to bring it back under control.

Cang Shubai said nothing more. He walked into the room and brought out the hot water bottle. Sure enough, she had secretly pried the spirit stone out of it again. He put the stone back in, walked out of the room, returned to her side, and tucked the item into her arms.

"If you get sick, you'll be complaining again that the medicine is bitter."

Mu Ran behaved herself, clutching the warming hot water bottle against her lower abdomen. With her listless expression, she looked rather pitiful.

Cang Shubai quietly and skillfully packed the small wooden parts on the table into a box. Glancing over, he noticed Mu Ran’s clenched hand and said, "Ranran."

Mu Ran turned slightly to the side, her posture clearly resistant.

Cang Shubai added, "You aren't feeling well, and making these little trinkets requires a great deal of mental effort. Give them to me."

Mu Ran lowered her head. "No."

Most of the time, she was very obedient to him, but there were occasional moments when her rebellious streak would be particularly strong.

Cang Shubai remained silent, just watching her quietly.

Mu Ran didn't know why; although her husband’s temper was always very good, the pressure he exerted whenever he put on this silent, unmoving expression was exceptionally strong.

She picked at the small object in her hand, then suddenly lifted her face. With curved brows and a beaming smile, she held out her hand to him. "Look, does it look like you?"

In her hand was a half-carved little wooden figure. Unlike the realistic style carved by other craftsmen, the little wooden figure she carved had a round face, a round body—in short, it looked chubby from head to toe, like a roly-poly toy. Yet, one could still discern the spirit of the person from the little figure's clothing and appearance.

The figure’s refined brows and eyes, combined with its serious expression and round, plump body, created a kind of contrasting cuteness.

Cang Shubai’s gaze fixed on the tiny wooden figure. Without even realizing it, the stern expression he had deliberately put on just moments ago was easily dismantled. His features softened with warmth and tenderness as his fingertips lightly touched the little wooden figure in her hand.

"Is it me?"

Mu Ran nodded. "Yes, is it cute?"

Cang Shubai took the little wooden figure and examined it carefully for a long time. His lips moved slightly. "Cute."

When he was young, his parents had bought him a wooden *moheluo* during the Qixi Festival; it was in the shape of a cute little child. He had liked it very much and kept it by his pillow. Later, after his parents passed away and their home was destroyed on that bloody night of the beast riot, that little *moheluo* had vanished without a trace.

As he grew older, he never thought to look twice at such trinkets that children liked.

Cang Shubai’s emotions were always muted, but having been married to him for so long, Mu Ran could still feel that he liked this little wooden figure.

He was happy, and so she was happy too.

Mu Ran rested her hands on the table, propping up her chin, and smiled as she watched the young man’s handsome profile. In the twilight, the light added a touch of haziness and softness to him, and she thought he looked even better.

When Cang Shubai lowered his eyes to look at her, he happened to meet his wife’s gaze, which was filled with joy.

The wind outside the window was moving, and the forest rustled, sounding quite lively.

Just like his heartbeat at this moment, it was exceptionally boisterous.

Cang Shubai reached out, his fingertips brushing the stray hair by Mu Ran’s temple behind her ear, but his pads lingered on her skin, reluctant to pull away. "Why did you suddenly think of making this?"

Mu Ran rubbed against his palm. "Last time we went to the lantern festival, there were children pestering their parents to buy them *moheluo*, and you took an extra look."

Cang Shubai was silent.

He had thought his emotions were always perfectly concealed, that he was no longer a child who needed these childish things, and he had assumed he hadn't taken an extra look. Little did he know that when he was in her company, he would relax all his disguises, exposing the emotions he would never show in front of others.

Mu Ran leaned closer to him, tilted her face up, and smiled softly. "Jinzhi is always indifferent to everything and shows no preferences. If you hadn't said you wanted to marry me back then, I really wouldn't have been able to tell that you liked me."

Thinking back, he would take the initiative to repair her leaking roof, bring her medicinal herbs when she was sick, and frequently "run into" her in the dark when she had to walk to town at night to negotiate business to make a living.

It turned out that his affection for her had long since left traces.

It was just that he held it in so tightly and was never one to express his feelings. If it hadn't been for a kind-hearted auntie coming to Mu Ran’s door to play matchmaker for a scholar in town, who knew when he would have finally spoken his mind.

Mu Ran hooked her little finger around Cang Shubai’s, shaking it gently as if in play, and laughed aloud. "You’re so awkward. If I weren't careful, I really wouldn't be able to guess whether you were happy or not. I really don't know what to do with you. To make our home better, I can only keep watching you like this, never missing a single move you make, so that I can know exactly what you like."

Just like the mung bean cakes; he would never say he liked eating such ordinary little pastries, and he would never take the initiative to mention what he needed. Whenever she asked what she liked or wanted, as for himself, he seemed to be completely...

chapters.title: The Wife’s Toy
chapters.content:
Mu Ran muttered, "After all, we are husband and wife. Often, I also want to satisfy your desires and make you happy."

The little finger she was hooking onto tightened slightly, entwining with hers. Soon, the man’s large hand enveloped her, rendering her mischievous hand unable to move.

She raised her face, meeting the man’s pitch-black eyes. They were like a deep abyss or a bottomless lake; beneath the calm exterior lurked surging undercurrents, rolling and galloping, threatening to shatter the facade of hypocritical tranquility and unleash a violent storm.

Mu Ran still remembered that on the day they were married, she had seen such eyes before.

That night, she had been worn out by the husband she had mistakenly thought was asexual.

But at this moment, it felt like an illusion, for Cang Shubai quickly returned to his usual calm and cold demeanor.

His hand circled her waist, pulling her into his embrace. He held her gently and with restraint, stroking the long hair at the back of her head, and whispered, "I like this little wooden figure very much. Thank you, Ranran."

Mu Ran came back to her senses and blinked. "As long as you like it. We are husband and wife, after all; you don't need to thank me."

Cang Shubai gave a low "Hmm" and asked her, "What would you like to eat tonight?"

"I want to eat Four-Joy Meatballs."

"Alright."

He patted the top of her head, his gaze lingering on her face for a moment before he stood up and walked into the kitchen. Not long after, the sounds of cooking could be heard from within.

Mu Ran touched her face with a sense of disappointment.

How strange. She had clearly felt that he wanted to kiss her just now; why did he just walk away?

Is it because we’ve been married for so long that I’m not as attractive as I used to be?

In the dead of night, when all was silent and the candles were extinguished, only the faint moonlight remained in the cozy house.

Cang Shubai looked at his sleeping wife, but he felt no drowsiness himself.

He reached out and touched her wrist again, his fingertips gently rubbing against it.

Her foundation was damaged, making it impossible for her to cultivate. As an ordinary person, she would only have a short lifespan of a hundred years.

Perhaps that was exactly why he had chosen her in the beginning, thinking that being husband and wife for a hundred years would be enough to help him pass the most difficult love trial in his cultivation breakthrough. He didn't know when it started, but a mere hundred years now felt far from enough.

He interlaced his fingers with hers, and warm spiritual energy flowed from his body into her bones and blood bit by bit.

Cang Shubai kissed the top of her head.

"A thousand years, ten thousand years, never to be parted."

In the courtyard, the Extreme Cold Fish, which was sleeping in the well like an ordinary fish, suddenly jumped out of the water. It transformed into a silver light, slipped in through the window, and hovered before its master.

Cang Shubai’s brows furrowed slightly.

The wind was strong at night, and the swaying tree shadows looked like ferocious ghosts baring their fangs and brandishing their claws.

Butcher Fan felt a chill in his heart and somewhat regretted agreeing to that old immortal. But thinking of the vast amounts of gold and silver treasures he would receive once the task was done, he dismissed his hesitation and walked firmly toward the ancient well under the old locust tree in the center of the village.

The village’s groundwater veins were interconnected; as long as he put the medicine here, the water of the entire village would be affected.

Butcher Fan looked around vigilantly. Seeing no one, he couldn't help but slap his own forehead.

"The immortal said I’m doing a good deed. If the village has a spiritual vein, everyone can become a cultivator. This is a great thing; why am I acting like I’m doing something shameful?"

He muttered to himself, took out the medicine bottle with peace of mind, and just as he opened the cap, he froze, his body stiff and unable to move.

Butcher Fan’s eyes widened in terror. Then, a silent, cyan-clad figure appeared before him.

He opened his eyes wide in horror, sweat pouring down his body, yet he could not utter a single word.

The medicine bottle entered the man in cyan’s hand. He poured out the powder and rubbed it between his fingertips. "Red Blood Powder to attract demonic beasts," he said.

Shock appeared in Butcher Fan’s eyes.

The man in cyan didn't spare him another glance. He pointed his sword-finger at the center of Butcher Fan’s brow. Suddenly, Butcher Fan felt a violent pain in his brain, as if it were being stirred; almost all the memories of his life surfaced.

When he was young, he peeked at Widow Zhang bathing and was caught and beaten up.

When he was older, he got entangled with the Li family’s wife and was caught and beaten up by her husband.

On his way back from the town’s apothecary, he encountered an old man lying by the roadside. The old man had an ethereal, scholarly air and claimed he was injured while hunting down a demonic cultivator who was plaguing the world. He gave Butcher Fan spirit stones, and that was how Butcher Fan brought him home to recover.

The old man said it was not appropriate to reveal his identity to avoid retaliation from the demonic cultivator. Butcher Fan, having received the spirit stones, believed him implicitly and told no one about the old man.

As for this bottle of medicine, it was also a "divine medicine" given to him by the old man.

And, in these memories, he frequently fantasized about the beautiful young Mistress Mu in the village.

The more memories the man in cyan viewed, the more painful Butcher Fan became, until the man’s brows darkened and he struck even harder.

Butcher Fan’s eyes rolled back, his stiff body trembling; his soul was clearly damaged.

Finally, the man in cyan lowered his hand.

Butcher Fan’s body went limp, and he collapsed to the ground.

The white-robed old man sat cross-legged in the humble room, closing his eyes to rest and continue repairing his injured body.

This small village didn't even have a spiritual vein, so his recovery was extremely slow. More and more cultivators were gathering in the town, and even Hong Fu from the Red Flame Peak had arrived. If he didn't plan ahead, he would surely be in danger.

The door opened and closed; it was Butcher Fan, greedy for money and lust, returning.

The old man opened his eyes and asked with a smile, "How did it go, my young friend?"

Butcher Fan said, "As the immortal instructed, the matter is settled."

"Good. You are indeed a person of destiny for me. Once the spiritual vein is formed, you will surely be blessed with great fortune."

Butcher Fan approached slowly. "I hope your words come true, Immortal."

He didn't stop his footsteps, continuing to move forward.

The old man frowned slightly. Just at this moment, Butcher Fan accelerated his pace. Flame-like cracks appeared on his skin, as if magma were burning and rolling inside his body.

With a boom, Butcher Fan’s body exploded. A scorching mist of blood mixed with searing heat waves shot into the sky, threatening to swallow the old man whole.

The old man instinctively summoned his life-bound artifact: a red plum and white snow umbrella spun open in mid-air. The ribs of the umbrella were made of thousand-year-old ice silkworm silk, and the canopy was woven with clouds and frost. Once opened, a biting, frigid chill spread across the sky, colliding violently with the incoming scalding blood mist and searing heat.

The old man’s old wounds had not yet healed, and as the heat wave struck, he spat out another mouthful of blood, but he managed to save his life.

A look of ruthlessness appeared in his eyes, but he deliberately said, "I wonder which fellow daoist is attacking from the shadows? Why not come out and meet? I still have many treasures here; perhaps I can gift them to you as a gesture of goodwill. Shall we be friends?"

The surrounding burning magma and flames were suddenly extinguished by a gust of cold wind. Absolute darkness descended, making it impossible to see one's own hand.

Cold blades arrived like lightning, the sound of them cutting through the air hidden within the darkness. They were fast to the extreme, sharp to the bone, and without any warning, they aimed straight for the old man’s vital point at the center of his brow.

The old man responded in a panic. The spiritual energy of the red plum and white snow umbrella surged into a barrier. Ice shards and cold blades collided with a harsh metallic clang, shaking the old man until his web between thumb and forefinger split, and a mouthful of blood nearly surged up.

But this was merely a feint.

A ghostly shadow swept past, faster than a stream of light. In the blink of an eye, the old man’s belongings accumulated over thousands of years, several life-saving spiritual treasures, and his Qiankun bag containing spiritual materials were all swept away by the black shadow, leaving not even a gap for him to resist.

The old man was shocked and furious, shouting sternly. The red plum and white snow umbrella unleashed all its power, sweeping out waves of frost and snow blades, but it only slashed at a void of shadow.

The next second, a domineering and sinister force slammed into his chest. The palm force, carrying an internal energy that burned the soul and eroded the bones, pierced through his spiritual shield and shattered several of his meridians.

"Puff—"

The old man spat out blood, his white clothes instantly stained crimson. The red plum and white snow umbrella vibrated with a hum, its spiritual energy dissipated, and it fell to the ground.

The old man knew he had encountered a god of death with unfathomable cultivation; staying meant certain death.

He gritted his teeth, bit his fingertip, and used his essence blood to activate a secret escape talisman. A pale golden light exploded around him, turning into a frantic streak of light that fled into the distance, not daring to look back even for his fallen artifact, leaving only a trail of blood.

The ice blade transformed from the Cold Fish wanted to chase, but at its master’s gesture, it flew back, turning into an ice-blue fish that circled its master’s side.

In the distance, a large group of cultivators was rushing over to hunt down the fleeing old man; there was no need for the person hidden in the dark to chase and expose himself.

He opened the stolen Qiankun bag and threw all the mediocre magic treasures to the Cold Fish as fish food. The Cold Fish ate its fill, its belly bulging, and it let out a burp, spitting out a few bubbles.

Then, the white jade red plum umbrella on the ground was picked up.

He moved his eyes slightly, and with a wave of his hand, this top-tier life-saving artifact transformed into the appearance of an ordinary oil-paper umbrella.

The Cold Fish rolled its eyes.

This person was planning to give the stolen treasure to his wife as a toy again.

Mu Ran had a good night’s sleep and only sat up lazily from the bed when the sun was high.

Hearing the sound, Cang Shubai entered the bedroom and sat by the bed, skillfully picking up a peach-pink dress to help her put it on. "I’ve cooked some porridge. Go wash up and have some to warm yourself."

Mu Ran was still a bit sleepy; she nodded sluggishly and naturally stretched out her feet, watching as Cang Shubai put on her shoes and socks.

The corner of her eye caught an extra umbrella on the table, and she looked puzzled.

"Jinzhi, when did we get an oil-paper umbrella?"

"The old one was worn out, so I bought a new one to better shield against the wind and rain." Cang Shubai gently held her ankle, put embroidered shoes on the socks he had just helped her put on, and said in a calm tone, "It didn't cost much. If you don't like it, just throw it away."

Mu Ran raised her head and opened her arms toward him. "That would be a waste. You’ve already bought it, so I’ll make good use of it."

Cang Shubai chuckled, picked her up, hung her in front of him, and patted her back.

"Go wash up; the porridge is getting cold."

Mu Ran leaned on his shoulder, smelling the scent on him, and closed her eyes comfortably and contentedly.

The Cold Fish in the well listened to the cloying sounds inside and boredly spat out two more bubbles.

I really don't understand what's so good about men and women always sticking together. Aren't they tired of being so mushy?

chapters.title: The Wooden Chick
chapters.content:
"There is no mistake about that disturbance; someone is definitely engaging in a magical duel!"

Numerous cultivators flew through the air, eyes scanning in all directions and ears alert to every sound, searching for the possible location of the Old Man of the Long Sword. However, the Old Man of the Long Sword was truly worthy of being an elder who had managed to survive for hundreds of years; his ability to hide was exceptionally superb. They had chased him all night without even catching a glimpse of his shadow.

Back in the day, when the Old Man of the Long Sword infiltrated the Void Secret Realm, he had plundered countless treasures. If they could capture him, those treasures on his person would naturally have to be "surrendered."

This was the reason why so many cultivators would rush to join the fray the moment they heard rumors of the Old Man of the Long Sword appearing in this remote area.

At this moment, a fragrant breeze wafted by, and everyone was drawn to the figure of a woman in red.

Hong Fu’s slender figure hovered in the air, her veil fluttering gently in the wind. Her eyes radiated spiritual power as she searched for any movement on the surrounding hills.

The Old Man of the Long Sword had once been her martial uncle and was very familiar with her methods, so he would naturally not be easily found by her. However, the area was surrounded by cultivators, so he certainly hadn't escaped yet.

A thought occurred to Hong Fu, and a bead of blood materialized in her hand.

This was blood that had flowed from the Old Man of the Long Sword when he was injured during their fight in the Void Secret Realm years ago.

For a cultivator, anything dropped by an opponent was worth collecting; it might come in handy one day. Now, this drop of the old man's blood had finally found its use.

A small, wooden, chubby chick flew into the air.

Many people were puzzled, wondering what kind of magical artifact Fairy Hong Fu had brought out.

After the wooden chick "tasted" the drop of blood, it opened its beak, let out a "chirp," and flapped its small wings, flying off in a certain direction.

Hong Fu followed without a word.

Yue Qingfeng had originally been ordered by his sect to assist Fairy Hong Fu in capturing the Old Man of the Long Sword, so seeing this, he hurriedly followed behind her.

The Old Man of the Long Sword was hiding in a temporarily found cave, regulating his breath and adjusting his energy.

His heart was filled with hatred and resentment; he almost ground his teeth to dust.

The rare treasures he had collected over hundreds of years had been snatched away by someone who had never even shown their face. It was as if all his hard work over the years had been in vain. What was even more infuriating was that the Qiankun bag had contained many magical artifacts he had risked being expelled from his sect to steal from the Void Secret Realm—items that would have been of great benefit to his future breakthroughs.

He had offended so many people and seized so many resources precisely because he had been stuck at the Nascent Soul stage for a long time. Seeing that he finally had hope of breaking through the Nascent Soul stage by piling up magical artifacts, he had been robbed of everything in one fell swoop. How could he not hate them?

He didn't know who it was that had fought him that night, but that person was truly insidious. They had come with the sole purpose of killing and looting, without any wasted words. This kind of underhanded behavior couldn't help but remind him of the man in green he had encountered in the secret realm two hundred years ago.

Could it be the man in green who had disappeared for two hundred years? Had he heard that he had appeared in this backwater and come to join the fun as well?

The Old Man of the Long Sword recalled being ambushed by the man in green in the secret realm back then, a wound that had never fully healed. He pressed his injured chest, feeling suspicious and uneasy.

But he had no time to continue thinking. A clumsy wooden chick suddenly flew into the cave and stopped in front of him.

The spiritual power of this wooden chick was very faint, not really a magical artifact, and it was precisely because of this that it was difficult to detect.

The Old Man of the Long Sword could not discern the origin of this wooden chick, but he quickly sensed that something was wrong.

He rose to flee, only to collide head-on with a fiery red long whip lashed toward him.

The whip burned with crimson flames; if one were careless enough to be struck by it, even if they didn't die, they would lose a layer of skin.

The Old Man of the Long Sword quickly dodged, and the whip landed on the stone wall, the immense force smashing several cracks into it.

Hong Fu’s figure appeared, her voice icy, "Old Man of the Long Sword, it’s been two hundred years. I’ve finally found you."

At the same time, a flying sword struck, and the Old Man of the Long Sword was nearly run through.

Yue Qingfeng stood beside Hong Fu, "Martial Uncle, this disciple is here to assist you."

Seeing Hong Fu’s two maidservants also blocking his path, the Old Man of the Long Sword thought to himself, *My life is in danger!*

"Martial Niece Hong Fu, I did guide your cultivation back then, after all. Can you truly show no regard for our past ties and let this old man go this once?"

If the Old Man of the Long Sword hadn't ambushed her back then, Hong Fu wouldn't have been injured and saved by the man in green. If she hadn't been saved by him, she wouldn't have let her guard down against a man for the first time in her life, and naturally, she wouldn't have been ridiculously thrown into a formation by that man to serve as a meat shield!

Hong Fu regarded the events of two hundred years ago as a supreme humiliation. If she didn't kill the Old Man of the Long Sword and the man in green, this knot in her heart would remain, and she would have no hope of breaking through her cultivation realm.

What past ties?

She only wanted to kill!

"In consideration of our time in the same sect, I will leave you with an intact corpse."

Before Hong Fu finished speaking, she exerted force from her wrist, and the crimson whip lashed out with a sharp, piercing sound. The whip was covered in barbs coated with cold poison, creating several scarlet blood blossoms in the air.

Yue Qingfeng followed closely behind. His long sword left its sheath like a dragon's roar, the sword light as cold as frost. His sword techniques were fast, accurate, and ruthless, each strike aiming directly at the old man's vital points.

With one whip and one sword, they trapped the Old Man of the Long Sword in the center.

The old man had already exhausted most of his cultivation. Facing their joint attack, he was already struggling to defend himself. He knocked away the tip of Hong Fu’s whip with his sword, then barely parried Yue Qingfeng’s thrust at his throat. The webbing between his thumb and forefinger split, blood gushing down the blade. He stumbled backward, his back hitting the cold stone wall; he had nowhere left to retreat.

His face was as pale as paper, and his eyes flashed with extreme terror and unwillingness. Knowing that continuing to fight would surely result in his death on the spot, his trembling fingers reached into his robe and gripped his last life-saving escape talisman.

The Old Man of the Long Sword bit his fingertip, using his remaining internal energy to activate the talisman. A golden light suddenly burst from the paper, and a pale golden glow enveloped his form, about to tear through the air and escape.

In an instant, an invisible force suddenly swept out from the shadows, faster than even light could follow. Carrying a ruthless power capable of crushing mountains and splitting stones, it slammed fiercely into the old man's kneecaps!

"Crack—"

A crisp and terrifying sound of bone breaking pierced the air. The old man's legs buckled, the bones shattering inch by inch. The excruciating pain made him let out a heart-wrenching scream. The talisman in his hand slipped away, and the light around him instantly dissipated.

Hong Fu lashed out with her whip, precisely wrapping it around the old man's neck and pulling it tight, while Yue Qingfeng held his long sword against the old man's heart, its cold glint menacing.

The Old Man of the Long Sword had lost any chance of escape.

He screamed, "Don't kill me! I have the man in gr—"

He wanted to say he had clues about the man in green, but a freezing chill from the shadows suddenly slashed his throat. Blood gushed out, and he collapsed to the ground, convulsing.

Hong Fu hurriedly used her spiritual power to stop the bleeding, protecting the old man's last shred of soul.

The Old Man of the Long Sword possessed many treasures; she couldn't let him die before he handed them all over.

Yue Qingfeng had already chased in the direction from which the chill had come. Under a tree, only a trace of cold energy remained. He returned to Hong Fu’s side with a heavy expression, "The person in the shadows is gone."

chapters.title: Two More Days
chapters.content:
Hong Fu looked at the old man with the long sword, who was now on his last breath on the ground, and her expression was not pleasant. "I didn't even notice that person's aura; they are a master."

The two maidservants exchanged a glance. One said, "Perhaps they also came for the old man's treasures."

The other maidservant knelt down and searched the old man's body. "Fairy, I didn't find his Qiankun bag."

Yue Qingfeng said, "Perhaps he hid it."

Hong Fu stared coldly at the old man gasping for breath on the ground. "It doesn't matter. His soul is in my hands; I have plenty of ways to make him hand it over."

After completing its mission, the wooden chick lost its luster, fell to the ground, and turned into a pile of scattered wood.

Yue Qingfeng sighed with emotion, "To think this inconspicuous little treasure had such a great effect; it is truly astonishing."

Hong Fu's heart stirred.

This little trinket—perhaps she really could try to get a few more into her possession.

"Oh my, that big fire at Butcher Fan's place really was strange!"

"The village head took people to look, and they say they couldn't even find any bones!"

"He was a man of crooked intentions to begin with. Which pretty girl in the surrounding ten miles hadn't he cast his greedy eyes upon? I reckon he must have offended some ruthless character, and they just burned him along with his house."

"That makes sense. So many cultivators have come to town lately, and there was a constant 'bang-bang-bang' sound on the hilltop last night. My husband said those must be people fighting with magic. Maybe Butcher Fan offended one of those cultivators and was killed for it."

The others clicked their tongues, sighing with emotion, though their sympathies were varied.

That is the way of the world; fights between cultivators are never rare. Sometimes, when ordinary people are caught in the crossfire, the latter can only consider themselves unlucky. After all, how many ordinary people in this world would dare to seek revenge against a cultivator?

The aunties huddled by the river washing water chestnuts chatted back and forth, exchanging the latest gossip in the village. However, today, what they talked about most was the fact that Butcher Fan had been blown to bits.

Mu Ran squatted to the side, listening with great interest, her speed in washing the water chestnuts slowing down considerably.

Auntie Wang nudged Mu Ran with her elbow and said, "I think Butcher Fan got what he deserved. You wouldn't know, but he loitered around your door several times, and every time he chose to come when your little doctor wasn't home."

As Mu Ran washed the water chestnuts, she couldn't help but peel the skin off, popped the white, fleshy fruit into her mouth, and mumbled, "Is that so?"

Auntie Wang said, "Isn't it? You girl are so lovely that you really attract trouble. I was even wondering if I should tell your little doctor about this so he could be more careful, but who would have thought Butcher Fan would be burned to nothing."

Mu Ran shook her head. "How terrifying."

Suddenly, someone shouted, "Little Lady Mu, your husband has come to pick you up again!"

At this shout, the others looked at Mu Ran and laughed teasingly.

Not far away, the young man stood tall and upright. The midwinter wind carried a chill, brushing past the ink-black strands of hair falling by his face. His green robes were simple, yet they accentuated his posture, straight as green bamboo. He was elegant and clear-minded, with a touch of warmth that seemed to have been steeped in a cold pool.

Before he even walked close, his gaze had already crossed the noisy crowd and settled steadily on Mu Ran. It was as if he could not see the laughter and teasing of the others, as if the bustle and noise of the crowd were not worth even half a glance compared to her looking up at him.

"The little doctor is here to pick her up again."

"Watching her so closely every day, as if the little lady is about to run away."

"If I had such a beautiful wife, I would watch her just as closely as the little doctor does."

The teasing from the others grew more lively. Mu Ran's face flushed, and she felt a bit embarrassed.

Cang Shubai walked over and gave a slight nod, acknowledging the group. When he reached Mu Ran's side, he took her cold hand, frowned slightly, and said, "Let's go home."

Mu Ran said "Oh," bid farewell to the aunties, picked up her basket, and followed Cang Shubai obediently.

Cang Shubai took the basket from her hand and glanced at the contents. "This stuff is a hassle to dig out of the ground, a hassle to wash, and a hassle to eat. It's so cold out; aren't you afraid of getting frostbite from soaking your hands in cold water for so long?"

Mu Ran's cold hands were held by his large ones, and as the warmth spread, she instantly forgot what the cold felt like.

She tilted her face up and said, "Old Man Zhang in the village planted half an acre of water chestnuts. He couldn't finish digging them, so he let us dig them for fun to take home as food. It's free, so it would be a waste not to."

Cang Shubai glanced again at the dozen or so water chestnuts in the basket. "Is this what you call 'a waste not to'?"

Mu Ran braced herself and said, "I really did dig a lot, it's just... it's just that I ate a lot too."

It was all the fault of those aunties and their vivid gossip. When she was listening intently, she couldn't help but start munching on them right there. If she hadn't remembered not to eat them all by herself, there wouldn't even be this handful left in the basket.

Cang Shubai asked her, "Coming back next time?"

She shook her head. "Not coming back."

He asked, "Why?"

"You're right, my hands are cold."

Cang Shubai chuckled softly and tucked her hands into his wide sleeves.

Back home, Cang Shubai first told Mu Ran to take a hot bath. She had been blowing in the cold wind by the river for so long, and he was afraid she would get sick.

After Mu Ran finished her bath and changed into clean clothes, she walked into the main room and was dazzled by the young man before her.

Cang Shubai sat in a chair, his eyes lowered. His long fingers held a knife with steady, light movements. As the purple skin of the water chestnut fell away, revealing the translucent flesh, it made his hands look even more slender and delicate, with distinct knuckles.

The handsome young man had a calm and refined expression, his profile soft. His focused demeanor was elegant and moving.

Cang Shubai had spent years rolling and crawling in the killing fields, making him exceptionally sensitive to the movements around him. He naturally noticed the girl staring at him without blinking.

However, he did not lift his eyes, focusing only on the work in his hands. It wasn't until the girl couldn't hold back any longer, thinking she was being clever as she quietly approached, hugged his waist from behind, and leaned on his back, that the corners of his lips curved upward.

Cang Shubai picked up a round, washed fruit from the water and brought it to her lips, which she swallowed in one bite.

He said, "Shall we stew some water chestnut sweet soup tonight?"

Mu Ran nodded. "Okay."

She deliberately rubbed her puffed-out cheeks against his face, clearly having another bout of clinginess. "Jinzhi, you are so good."

Cang Shubai asked, "On which day am I not good?"

Mu Ran laughed out loud. "You are good every day, but tomorrow's Jinzhi will always be even better than today's Jinzhi."

Cang Shubai set down what he was holding, wiped his hands with a cloth, turned around, and pulled her into his arms. Mu Ran sat on his lap, and his hand reached out to gently stroke her cheek.

"So, will you like me more tomorrow than you do today?"

Mu Ran squinted her eyes comfortably. Perhaps it was because she had eaten the sweet water chestnut, but her voice was much sweeter too. "Yes, I will like you a little more every day."

Cang Shubai chuckled. Thinking that her reaction to her period was no longer as intense as it had been in the past few days, he lifted her chin and finally kissed the corners of her lips again.

It started with a simple touch, then a gentle caress, and then, with her tacit and familiar cooperation, the warmth successfully slipped in, tangling with her tongue, exchanging breaths until they could no longer be distinguished from one another.

After a long while, he pulled back slightly, yet remained pressed against her lips.

"Two more days."

That was the day her period would end.

Mu Ran's eyes sparkled. She leaned into his ear and whispered something softly.

Cang Shubai's gaze was deep. He caught her right hand, pressed a light kiss to her fingertips, and his voice was slightly hoarse. "Good."

chapters.title: Chapter 15 You Are So Kind
chapters.content:
It turns out that some things should not be promised lightly.

Mu Ran had overestimated herself; after working for a long time, she was nowhere near finishing.

In the end, she grew impatient and dove under the quilt.

The young man was caught completely off guard, and that was how he suffered a total defeat.

A short while later, he fished her out and took her to wash up.

Cang Shubai’s tall, slender frame seemed to still be radiating heat. "Don't ever do that again."

Mu Ran was puzzled. "Why can you do that to me, but I can't do it to you?"

She was simply following his lead.

Cang Shubai met her innocent gaze, his throat involuntarily going dry. He shifted his eyes away, feeling uncomfortable, avoiding her overly direct stare.

Mu Ran, however, would not let him off. She clung to his embrace. "I like you, so I want to make you happy. Besides, wasn't Jinzhi also quite comf—"

He covered her mouth.

Mu Ran couldn't say another word.

Cang Shubai picked her up and placed her on the bed, lying down under the quilt with her. He patted the top of her head. "Sleep."

Mu Ran: "Oh."

She closed her eyes, satisfied with the success of her mischief. What she didn't tell him was that the more gentle, refined, mature, and steady he was in his daily life, the more she wanted to see him lose his cool composure and become utterly chaotic.

Hmm, it was truly a sense of accomplishment.

The next morning, Mu Ran climbed out of bed, letting Cang Shubai pick out the dress he liked from the wardrobe and dress her, as he always did.

Having been married to Cang Shubai for nearly two years, she had discovered some of his preferences.

He liked her to wear brightly colored dresses. The wardrobe was filled with colorful clothes, and it could be said that two-thirds of the space was occupied by her things. As for himself, he wore the same few outfits back and forth; his material desires were very low.

Cang Shubai tidied the girl’s long hair, looking at her before him, a gentle smile spreading in his eyes.

The goose-yellow ru-skirt set off her skin, which was fairer than snow, as if it had been kneaded from the most tender glow of spring. Wrapped in the warm sunlight, it clung to her body, but when she smiled, the light in her eyes was even brighter than the patterns on her clothes—she was the very picture of someone who was cherished and full of life.

Cang Shubai said, "From now on, when you go to town, we go together."

Mu Ran was stunned. "Huh?"

Cang Shubai leaned down, getting closer to her, and deliberately pinched her cheek. "I know you’ve been secretly going to the town workshop to do business."

Mu Ran played dumb. "Have I? I don't think so, you must be mistaken."

Cang Shubai watched her performance quietly.

Mu Ran lowered her head, feeling guilty, and wound the ribbon on her dress around her finger. "I just... I just went once or twice, that's all."

"Just occasionally?"

Mu Ran pursed her lips, and giving up on the charade, she looked up and said, "Fine, maybe I went a little bit more frequently, but this is absolutely not because I look down on you or think you earn too little money."

He picked her up and placed her on the chair in front of the vanity, picked up a wooden comb, and combed her hair with gentle movements, yet he continued to press her as if he wouldn't let the matter go. "If it's not because you think I earn too little, then what is it for?"

Mu Ran looked at him in the mirror and said slowly, "I have hands and feet too, and I can earn money to help with household expenses. I want to save a little more money to manage our home better, so you won't have to go out late at night to find medicinal herbs just for that little bit of extra pay."

Cang Shubai’s hand, which was stroking her hair, paused slightly. A surge of heat inexplicably welled up inside him, one that was difficult to soothe.

He said, "You don't like me going out at night."

"I don't." Mu Ran turned to face him, lifting her face, her dark, moist eyes sparkling with glints of light. "The mountain forest at night is dangerous. Every time you go out at night, I can't close my eyes or fall asleep. I'm afraid something will happen to you."

Cang Shubai’s occasional night outings were nothing more than to kill people and seize treasures; most of the enemies from those years had already been dealt with by him.

He had long since broken through the Nascent Soul stage and reached the Void Refinement stage. There were very few people who could be his match, but above Void Refinement, there were still the Mahayana and Tribulation stages. There is always someone better, and there is always a heaven beyond heaven; it was hard to guarantee he wouldn't encounter a more powerful opponent in the future.

But he was a man who knew how to judge the situation best—if he couldn't win, he would run. It wasn't that easy to make him die.

However, he couldn't tell Mu Ran this.

Cang Shubai inserted a butterfly-shaped bead hairpin into her hair, his fingertips lightly moving the butterfly's wings. He gazed into her eyes, tenderness blooming between his brows, and said softly, "I promise you, I won't go out to pick herbs at night anymore."

Mu Ran was overjoyed. "Really?"

Cang Shubai nodded. "Really."

She hugged his waist happily. "Jinzhi, you are so kind."

Mu Ran’s smiling face fell into his eyes, shining brightly, charming and moving.

He thought, she was wrong.

It was clearly she who was so kind.

Since everything had been said, there was no need for Mu Ran to wait for him to leave before sneaking off to town. Today, Cang Shubai took her out with him. Upon arriving in the bustling town, they heard many people discussing.

"The 'Old Man Longsword,' who had disappeared for two hundred years, was finally caught by Fairy Hongfu."

"I heard that Old Man Longsword plundered quite a few treasures in the Void Secret Realm back then. Fairy Hongfu must have gained a lot this time."

"She has been stuck at the Nascent Soul stage for two hundred years; perhaps this time she will really reach the point of breakthrough. If Red Flame Peak gains another Void Refinement cultivator, the other sects will only be left in the dust."

Mu Ran heard the pedestrians' conversation, thinking only that the person these cultivators were looking for had already been found, and if only they could leave this small place quickly.

Suddenly, a bag of warm pastries was placed in her hand.

Cang Shubai said, "Eat something if you're hungry. Don't work too hard. I'll come to pick you up after I finish work."

Mu Ran nodded and smiled. "I know, go ahead and get to work."

After Cang Shubai turned and left, Mu Ran walked briskly into the Song family workshop. Boss Song had already been standing on tiptoes looking out the door for a while. Seeing Mu Ran enter, he couldn't help but tease her with a smile.

"Young people really are affectionate. Even saying goodbye has to be so lingering, as if you won't see each other tomorrow."

Mu Ran’s cheeks flushed slightly. "It's not as exaggerated as you say. I still have things to finish, I won't talk to you anymore, I have to get to work."

She hurried into the back workshop, not giving anyone a chance to tease her further.

Boss Song wanted to laugh a bit more, but thinking that Mu Ran working meant earning money for him, he dismissed the idea.

In the medical clinic on the other side, Dr. Hu was filling a prescription for another patient.

Cang Shubai arrived late and entered from the door.

In front of the patient, Dr. Hu pointed at Cang Shubai and cursed, "You finally know to come to work? Several waves of patients have already come, and you were nowhere to be seen. I pay you to work, not to enjoy yourself! I'm warning you, if you're late again tomorrow, you won't get your wages for this month!"

Cang Shubai had an excellent temper; he didn't argue and began to organize the medicine in the cabinet conscientiously.

chapters.title: Sugar Pills
chapters.content:
Once the patients had left and there were no outsiders in the medical clinic, Dr. Hu’s attitude underwent a complete transformation.

"Godfather, just leave those things there; let me tidy up!" Dr. Hu wore a fawning smile as he snatched the medicinal herbs from Cang Shubai’s hands, laughing incessantly. "You go sit down and rest."

Cang Shubai asked, "Any news from town?"

Dr. Hu quickly replied, "Hong Fu has managed to keep the old man Chang Jian alive, wanting to interrogate him about where those treasures are hidden. However, I overheard the sound of a cup shattering in Hong Fu’s room last night; I’m afraid she didn’t get what she wanted."

Cang Shubai said, "Continue."

Dr. Hu went on, "I investigated the man who died after transforming into a demonic beast that day. He was a resident of the neighboring town. There have been reports of people going missing in the vicinity lately; I fear they have all been captured by demonic cultivators to be refined into demonic beasts."

Cang Shubai asked, "Did the disappearances only start after these cultivators appeared?"

Dr. Hu nodded. "Exactly. But I haven't been able to find out who is behind such wicked deeds. Godfather, should we intervene?"

Cang Shubai opened the medicine cabinet, took out a few herbs, and said nonchalantly, "As long as they don't disturb the peace here, there is no need to interfere."

Dr. Hu knew that Cang Shubai was neither purely righteous nor purely evil. To put it bluntly, he was simply indifferent to everything as long as his own interests were not compromised.

Cang Shubai possessed no sense of justice and no compassion; he truly had a talent for the Path of Ruthlessness.

Dr. Hu looked at the herbs Cang Shubai had taken out and asked curiously, "Godfather, what kind of medicine are you planning to make?"

"Soul-Nourishing Pills."

"For Godmother?"

Cang Shubai gave a hum of affirmation, walked to the side with the herbs, placed them in a mortar, and ground them into a fine powder with a pestle.

Soul-Nourishing Pills were of little use to cultivators, but for ordinary people, they could prolong life.

The century-old Yellow Yan Grass, the thousand-year-old Flood Dragon Gall, the ninth-grade Soul-Condensing Flower... these were all extremely precious treasures for nourishing the soul. For an ordinary cultivator, seeing even one of these would be a stroke of immense luck; gathering a full set was as difficult as ascending to heaven.

Yet, these herbs, which many cultivators would use to break through their cultivation realms, were being used by Cang Shubai to make ordinary Soul-Nourishing Pills?

When Cang Shubai first decided to marry, he had agreed to be a husband to a mortal woman for only a hundred years, intending to pass a trial of love, gain insight into life and death, and temper his state of mind.

But now, he was feeding her Soul-Nourishing Pills—this hardly looked like someone who only intended to be a husband for a hundred years!

Dr. Hu’s eyes widened, finding it inconceivable.

It’s over. This demon seems to have truly fallen in love.

Cang Shubai commanded without looking up, "Bring the sugar jar over."

Dr. Hu: "...Huh?"

He raised his eyes. "Ranran cannot handle bitterness. Go get the sugar."

Dr. Hu: "..."

With a hollow gait and a sense of existential doubt, he turned around and obediently went to fetch the sugar jar.

Mu Ran was hunched over, staring at a small wooden dog on her workbench that had collapsed after walking only a few steps, rubbing her chin in thought.

"Where exactly did it go wrong? Why can it only walk three steps before collapsing and stopping? Is it a structural issue, or is the spirit stone insufficient?"

Boss Song suddenly shouted from outside, "Little Mu, there is a guest who wants to see you!"

Mu Ran responded, set aside her work for the moment, and walked out quickly.

Standing in the shop was a young woman dressed in an extraordinary manner. She was examining the items displayed in the workshop. Upon seeing Mu Ran, she scrutinized her from head to toe, perhaps finding her plain and ordinary, and looked quite disappointed.

Boss Song whispered to Mu Ran, "This is a maidservant who follows Fairy Hong Fu. That is the legendary Fairy Hong Fu! So many people want to speak a single word to her and cannot; you are lucky, girl."

Mu Ran asked politely, "Is there something you need from me, Miss?"

The young woman conjured a pile of wooden parts in her hand. "Did you make these?"

Mu Ran looked at them for a moment, nodded, and said, "I made them."

"It only worked once before this 'paging chicken' broke. Your craftsmanship doesn't seem to be very good."

Mu Ran thought to herself that if a paging chicken could be used infinitely, how would anyone buy new ones, and how would she make money?

But she couldn't say such things, so she could only smile and say, "I am just an ordinary artisan; naturally, I cannot compare to those master craftsmen who can forge magical treasures. It is just a small trinket; please don't laugh at my incompetence."

Most cultivators held a sense of superiority over ordinary people. This young woman was a respectful maid in front of Fairy Hong Fu, but she carried an air of arrogance in front of ordinary people.

Mu Ran could understand it to some extent; it was the environment. The rules of this world were just like that.

Those with less power than oneself were ants.

Those with power equal to one's own were fellow Daoists.

Those with power exceeding one's own were seniors.

In the eyes of many, Mu Ran remained at the level of an ant.

The young woman said in a commanding tone, "My Fairy wants to order three of these paging chickens. Deliver them to the Yueran Inn tomorrow."

Mu Ran said with difficulty, "Miss, the process of making these paging chickens is quite troublesome. Making three in one day is really..."

"Once the task is done, you will be rewarded with five hundred spirit stones."

Mu Ran: "I'll do it. I will definitely get them done. The Yueran Inn, right? I’ve noted it down. I will definitely deliver them on time tomorrow."

People in this mundane world, as expected, were mostly blinded by money.

The young woman did not linger any longer and turned to leave.

Boss Song worriedly asked, "Can you really manage to make three in one day?"

Mu Ran was confident. "It's fine, I'll just stay up all night."

That was five hundred spirit stones! She might not even earn that much in over half a year.

Mu Ran had already planned it out. With this money, she could buy a few more life-saving talismans, giving her another layer of security to survive in this dangerous world.

At dusk, Cang Shubai arrived at the workshop to pick her up.

Mu Ran came out carrying her toolbox and smiled when she saw him. "Were there more patients today? You finished work a little later than usual."

Cang Shubai took the toolbox from her hands. "There were a few more patients."

In truth, it was because he had spent some time preparing the medicine.

He placed a wooden sugar box into her hands. "I saw someone selling sugar pills on the road. You like sweets, so I bought a box."

Mu Ran said, "I'm not a child anymore. You still buy me sugar pills? If the aunts in the village find out, they’ll tease me again."

"Then shall I throw them away?"

"No!" Mu Ran protected the sugar box with both hands. "You’ve already bought them. Since you spent the money, I will finish them properly."

She opened the box, which was filled with round, black pills. They didn't look like much, but she popped one into her mouth, tasted the sweetness, and squinted her eyes in enjoyment.

She clearly liked them, yet she said, "Jinzhi, you mustn't spend money recklessly in the future."

Cang Shubai’s eyes curved slightly. "Alright."

When they reached a deserted area, he took her hand. Feeling that the toolbox in her other hand was somewhat heavy, he asked softly, "Why did you bring your tools home today?"

"I took on a big order. The customer is in a hurry, so I have to work hard to get it done today."

"A big order?"

"Yes! It’s five hundred spirit stones. After splitting the profit with Boss Song, I’ll still earn quite a lot!" Mu Ran hugged his arm. When there were no outsiders around, she loved to cling to him and stay close.

She smiled brightly. "I’ve already decided. Once I get the money, I’m going to the talisman shop to buy the most expensive talismans—the ones from Biyun Mountain. The talismans from that mountain have the best life-saving effects. I’ll put them into a peace charm for you to wear, so even if you have to go out in the future, I can feel a bit more at ease."

Cang Shubai asked, "How do you know that the talismans from Biyun Mountain have the best life-saving effects?"

Mu Ran’s eyes drifted, and then she smiled. "I asked the owner at the talisman shop. He said Biyun Mountain’s are the best, so they must be."

Cang Shubai gripped her hand tightly. "Ranran, I don't need them. You’ve saved so much money; you can use it to buy things you want for yourself."

"What I want most is for you to be safe, for me to be safe, and for our home to be safe."

Cang Shubai’s long eyelashes trembled slightly, unable to hide the surging emotions in his eyes.

His tall figure leaned forward slightly, bowing his head with unmistakable tenderness.

He planted a light kiss on the corner of Mu Ran’s lips.

She looked up at him, her eyes shining brightly.

Cang Shubai’s Adam’s apple bobbed, and it finally turned into a soft chuckle. "Let's go home."

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.content:
To earn that massive sum of five hundred spirit stones, Mu Ran truly lit the candles, prepared to pull an all-nighter.

Fearing she would disturb Cang Shubai’s rest, she specifically moved her things into the main room. She covered the table with a pile of tools, assembling and calibrating the wooden chicks bit by bit.

Late at night, Cang Shubai, draped in a loose cyan robe, stood at the bedroom doorway and asked softly, "Will this take much longer?"

Mu Ran didn't even look up as she replied, "There are still two paging chicks left to make. Jinzhi, you go ahead and rest. I’ll go to bed once I’m finished."

A moment later, she didn't hear the sound of the bedroom door closing. Instead, a tall figure appeared beside her, almost enveloping her entirely.

Mu Ran raised her face and collided with the youth’s deep, dark eyes.

He said, "I’ll help you."

Mu Ran was skeptical. "You... help me?"

Cang Shubai was silent for a moment. "Am I not capable?"

Mu Ran quickly said, "Of course you are!"

She laid out the blueprints and placed a pile of wooden materials in front of him. "Jinzhi, help me assemble these parts according to the diagrams."

Mu Ran thought to herself that putting together wooden chicks based on blueprints was just like playing with building blocks; it shouldn't be difficult. She could just calibrate them later, and it would be fine.

Suddenly, she felt a bit puzzled.

What are building blocks?

Cang Shubai glanced at the blueprints and first picked up the largest wooden piece. Among the pile of tiny components, he found another small piece of wood. The parts had grooves or protrusions; if placed correctly, two pieces could fit together seamlessly.

This kind of thing was indeed not difficult.

Cang Shubai’s skills in alchemy and refining magical treasures were beyond question; this sort of puzzle-like task should certainly be a piece of cake.

However, when it came to picking up the fine threads made of ground spirit stone powder to string through the bodies of the wooden chicks, he had to look at the blueprints several times, and his movements became much slower. It took him a long time just to thread one strand into a wooden chick’s body.

Then, with a "pop," the thread caught fire and burned away.

Mu Ran shrieked, "My circuit!!!"

Cang Shubai instinctively realized he had caused trouble. With a wave of his hand, the fire was extinguished, but the wooden chick had been scorched black. He stood there at a loss, watching Mu Ran hold her head and wail.

In the two years since she married him, Mu Ran’s emotions had always been stable.

This was the first time he had seen her in such a state of painful screaming.

Mu Ran grabbed his arm, stood on tiptoe to look at the scorched wooden bird in his hand, and said, on the verge of tears, "That was a circuit I spent so long rolling out, and it’s burned away."

Cang Shubai asked cautiously, "A circuit?"

"It’s the line that transmits spiritual power. You have to grind spirit stones into powder first, then add Tuoluo flower juice, and very carefully roll them into threads as thin as a strand of hair. You also have to ensure the entire thread is of uniform thickness, otherwise, the effect of conducting the spirit stone’s power will be greatly diminished!"

Cang Shubai looked at the object in his hand as if it were a hot potato.

Mu Ran took the damaged wooden chick with a pained heart and let out a heavy sigh. But upon noticing the silent Cang Shubai, she looked up and suddenly revealed a brilliant smile.

"It’s okay, it’s just one damaged section. My skills are so good, I can fix it."

She placed the item on the table, disassembled the parts, set the burned section aside, and carefully examined what she had left, pondering how to find a substitute.

Cang Shubai said, "Ranran, I’m sorry."

"It’s okay, it’s okay. You didn't do it on purpose. Besides, I’m at fault too; I didn't explain it clearly to you. I can’t blame you."

As Mu Ran spoke, she looked up again, her eyes bright and her voice light. "I’m hungry. Could you go cook me a bowl of noodles for a late-night snack?"

Cang Shubai knew she was deliberately finding something for him to do so he wouldn't feel useless. Looking at the thing he had destroyed, he said in a low voice, "Alright."

When he reached the kitchen door, he couldn't help but look back.

Mu Ran was looking down, working quietly in the candlelight. The warm yellow light spilled from the candle, softening the contours of her profile, her eyelashes casting small, shallow shadows beneath her eyes that fluttered gently as she lowered her head.

Cang Shubai suddenly felt that if she had scolded him a few times, he might have felt better.

Mu Ran truly pulled an all-nighter, only finishing the three paging chicks when the sky began to brighten. Too tired to tidy up the mess on the table, she collapsed onto the bed and fell asleep instantly.

After sleeping for only an hour, she forced herself to crawl back up to go to town with Cang Shubai.

Cang Shubai fed her a sugar pill. Perhaps the power of sweets was great, as her weary body felt a bit better. Cang Shubai specifically arranged to meet Uncle Zhao, who was also heading to town to deliver firewood, and paid a small fee to hitch a ride on his donkey cart.

Mu Ran sat on the donkey cart, leaning against Cang Shubai, and closed her eyes to sleep for a while longer, though the cart was bumpy, so she didn't sleep very well.

Uncle Zhao drove the cart, laughing heartily. "Little doctor, you two are truly a loving couple."

Cang Shubai responded, holding Mu Ran’s hand and quietly channeling warm spiritual power into her. The furrow in Mu Ran’s brow slowly smoothed out, and she was able to get some good sleep despite the bumps.

Cang Shubai first dropped Mu Ran off at the Song family workshop, promising to come pick her up later, before heading to the clinic to "start work," albeit late again.

Taking advantage of the lack of people, Doctor Hu scurried over to flatter him. "Godfather, I’ve obtained some wonderful, rare treasures. They are perfect for longevity and health. I offer them all to you, Godfather."

He presented a storage bag filled with medicinal herbs he had collected over the years; taking out any one of them in the outside world would incite many to fight over it.

Cang Shubai never refused things he could use. He accepted the bag and said, "You are about to break through to the Golden Core stage, aren't you?"

Doctor Hu nodded. "Yes, I am."

A medicine bottle appeared in Cang Shubai’s hand, which he tossed to Doctor Hu. "These Foundation-Consolidating Pills will be useful to you."

Doctor Hu opened the bottle and took a look; they were all top-tier pills. He was overjoyed and said repeatedly, "Thank you, Godfather! You are the person I love and respect the most. I will definitely serve you and Godmother well!"

He thought to himself, it really is better to have a Godmother.

In the past, no matter how he tried to flatter this "star of misfortune," his attitude had always been indifferent.

Today, he had only brought out herbs useful to the Godmother, and this "star" had given him such a huge reward!

Having followed this man for a hundred years, he had finally found the right way to please him.

Doctor Hu was happy, but couldn't help but glance a few more times at the object in Cang Shubai’s hand. "Godfather, do you dislike spirit stones so much that you use them to play with fire?"

chapters.title: Summer Insects Cannot Discuss Ice
chapters.content:
Just as Dr. Hu finished speaking, the mixture of spirit stone powder and Tuoluo flower juice in Cang Shubai’s hand sparked again, finally emitting a wisp of black smoke before vanishing.

Cang Shubai remained silent.

Dr. Hu was bewildered, but after glancing at Cang Shubai’s expression, he dared not say anything more.

Since entering the clinic today, Cang Shubai had been grinding spirit stones into powder and crushing Tuoluo flowers, with small flames flickering incessantly.

Was he practicing some strange new technique again?

After a while, Cang Shubai wiped the black ash from his hands with a handkerchief and asked, "In the craft of artisans, have you ever heard of the term 'circuit'?"

Dr. Hu shook his head. "Never heard of it."

At the mention of artisans, Dr. Hu’s eyes darted. "Is this related to my godmother? Are you trying to make something for her, Godfather?"

Cang Shubai did not reply.

Dr. Hu suddenly felt an urge to laugh.

This fierce man practiced unconventional paths—alchemy, forging, talismans... he dabbled in everything. Although his talent wasn't the absolute best, he was ruthless with himself and had cunningly acquired many secret manuals, allowing him to perform well in every field.

Dr. Hu had assumed he was omnipotent; it turned out there were things he couldn't handle either.

He cleared his throat. "Godfather, as the saying goes, there is a specialty in every trade..."

"Do you know what a circuit is?"

Dr. Hu: "...I do not."

Cang Shubai picked up his things and left. "Summer insects cannot discuss ice."

Dr. Hu: "..."

What is there to be so arrogant about?

If it weren't for Godmother, wouldn't you be just as clueless!

Dr. Hu grumbled inwardly, but he didn't dare say it aloud, picking up a rag to clean.

Mu Ran arrived at Yueran Inn carrying her toolbox. The proprietor had long since received instructions, and upon hearing she was there to deliver goods to Fairy Hongfu, he personally led her to the second floor, to the Heaven-grade guest room.

Suddenly, the terrifying sound of a whip lashing came from inside the room, followed by a "thud" as someone collapsed to the floor.

Both the proprietor and Mu Ran shuddered.

Mu Ran looked at the proprietor, asking with her eyes.

The proprietor shook his head, signaling that he dared not speculate about an immortal.

A maid’s voice came from inside: "Who is it?"

The proprietor quickly replied: "It is Mistress Mu here to deliver the items the Fairy ordered."

Before long, the door opened. The maid who had visited the workshop last time glanced at Mu Ran and said, "Come in."

Mu Ran stepped into the room, and the door closed behind her.

The room was filled with the smell of blood. An old man lay on the floor, covered in blood and lacerations. It was unclear what spell had been cast upon him, but his soul was floating outside his body, bound by chains. The soul glowed a scorching red, as if being burned by flames, and was in immense agony.

Faintly, Mu Ran could smell something burning. She instinctively covered her nose and mouth, not daring to look further.

"You have quite the nerve, not collapsing to the ground or screaming."

The woman’s voice was ethereal and melodic, laced with a careless indifference.

Mu Ran looked up.

The woman in red wore a veil, revealing only a pair of cold, shimmering eyes. Her irises were light in color, and her gaze held no warmth as it swept over her—a mere gesture of condescension. Even with the lower half of her face hidden, her haughty, high-and-mighty air remained undiminished.

Mu Ran said, "I had heard of the Fairy’s great name before coming here. To see an immortal whom ordinary people rarely encounter in a lifetime is a great honor for me; thus, I felt only excitement and nervousness, leaving no room for anything else."
