Hongfu had heard many compliments and was unmoved by Mu Ran’s words, though her gaze lingered on Mu Ran’s face for a moment longer.

Mu Ran was exceptionally bright and moving, her features soft and relaxed yet not appearing weak. Her eyes were as clear as water, holding a faint, quiet shimmer when she looked at you, unflinching and steady. With only a touch of makeup, she possessed a clean, transparent quality.

Hongfu asked, "Have we met somewhere before?"

Mu Ran shook her head. "If I had met the Fairy, I would surely remember it for the rest of my life. Today is indeed my first time meeting you."

Hongfu suspected she was overthinking it and asked directly, "Where are the things I wanted?"

Mu Ran opened her toolbox and took out the three "paging chickens." The two maids took them and presented them to Hongfu for inspection.

Hongfu took one look, withdrew her gaze, and felt a rare spark of curiosity. "How did you think of making these little trinkets? As far as I know, even the items made by master forgers are not necessarily as interesting as these toys of yours."

Mu Ran replied, "I was just idle and occasionally had small ideas. I didn't expect that when I tried to make them, they would actually work. I never imagined that the little trinkets I made would one day catch the eye of a Fairy."

Hongfu had other thoughts.

Mu Ran was talented. If she offered her an opportunity and recommended her to cultivate at Zhushen Mountain, perhaps she could be of use in the future.

But after looking Mu Ran up and down, she quickly dismissed the idea.

Mu Ran had no spiritual roots; she would never achieve greatness.

That was true—among the masses of this world, most were mediocre. How many geniuses like Hongfu could there be?

Before the sun had set, Cang Shubai left the clinic early again. He went to the Song family workshop but did not find her.

Boss Song said, "Mistress Mu went to Yueran Inn to deliver things to Fairy Hongfu. Didn't the young doctor know?"

Hongfu.

Cang Shubai’s brows furrowed slightly, and he turned to leave.

The closer he got to the inn, the more restless the Cold Fish hidden in his sleeve became, sensing its master’s suppressed emotions.

Was it a coincidence, or a scheme?

Cang Shubai’s dark eyes were like calm, stagnant water, but deep within the darkness, turbulent currents were already surging.

Until a girl in a green dress walked out of the inn, her eyes lighting up when she saw him, calling out with a smile, "Jin-zhi!"

She ran lightly, her skirt swaying gently. Her clear eyes reflected only him, her brows curving into a warm moon, her smile as bright as crushed starlight.

Cang Shubai’s heart, which had been submerged at the bottom of a cold pool, suddenly resumed its normal rhythm. He reached out to catch her as she hurried over, holding her slightly cold hands. As he slowly warmed them, the undercurrents in his eyes faded, replaced by tenderness.

Mu Ran picked up a money pouch and shook it, the sound of coins jingling inside. She shared her joy with him. "There are five hundred extra spirit stones in here! My pouch could barely hold them. On the way back, let’s go to Xuanbao Pavilion and buy a better-quality pouch that can hold more things."

Cang Shubai took her toolbox and gently stroked her hair. "As you wish."

Mu Ran smiled, grabbed his hand, and started walking back, muttering, "We should also buy a Qiankun bag. That way, when you go to gather herbs, you won't have to carry a basket; it will be much more convenient. Also, we must have a good meal tonight. Let’s go buy a few pounds of meat and some ribs later to make the sweet and sour pork ribs you like."

Cang Shubai said, "Sweet and sour pork ribs are what you like."

"Oh, we are husband and wife, why distinguish between you and me? What I like must be what you like, right?" She tilted her head up, her bright eyes blinking, with stars flickering within them.

Cang Shubai’s eyes curved slightly. "Right."

Mu Ran laughed happily.

In the room on the second floor of the inn, the smell of blood and burning was even more intense.

A maid said, "Fairy, the old man Changjian still refuses to open his mouth and reveal the location of the treasure."

The soul of the old man Changjian was beyond tears.

It wasn't that he refused to open his mouth!

It was because when his throat was slit, a restriction was placed upon him. As long as he tried to speak of his treasure being stolen, he couldn't make a sound. Even if he tried to pick up a pen to write, his body would go stiff, unable to reveal any relevant information.

Hongfu stood by the window, watching the young couple disappear into the crowd below. A strange feeling arose in her heart, flashing by so quickly she couldn't grasp it.

She remembered visiting Biyun Mountain ten years ago. At that time, she had seen a seven-year-old girl holding a bell, strangely saying "hello, hello, hello," with a pile of tools at her feet.

The girl loved tinkering with little trinkets, somewhat resembling the Mu Ran she had seen today.

But Mu Ran had no roots for cultivation, and her husband also showed no signs of any cultivation base.

Hongfu couldn't help but think that perhaps she was just overthinking it.

She turned around and looked at the old man Changjian, whose soul was about to be torn apart. "If he refuses to speak, keep torturing him until he does."

The old man Changjian really wanted to cry out loud.

chapters.title: Nightmare (Part 1)
chapters.content:
After returning home, Mu Ran climbed straight into bed to catch up on some sleep.

Having earned such a large sum of money, she slept with exceptional satisfaction and peace, even drifting into a dream.

In the dream, she slept for a long time in a place where the water met the sky. She sat up and stretched comfortably, and upon opening her eyes, she saw shimmering waves, as if she were in a fairyland on earth.

Confused, she stood up and walked slowly through a world that seemed to have no end. In the blink of an eye, she saw a familiar figure.

The man stood at the edge of the hazy light and mist, his black robes hanging down like ink, moving without wind, making the surrounding air feel a few degrees heavier.

Most striking was his long hair; it was not the usual frost-white, but rather like cold snow that had fallen and never melted, or perhaps like crushed moonlight, cascading from his shoulders, each strand distinct, emitting a cold luster in the dim world.

He had originally stood as still as a cold stone, his brows and eyes frozen in an impenetrable silence. But the moment he saw her, the coldness around him seemed like a sheet of ice suddenly pierced, shattering and dissolving bit by bit.

The depths of those eyes, usually so indifferent, suddenly surged, flashing with a look of incredulous shock, and once they locked onto her, they could no longer look away.

"Jinzhi?" Mu Ran asked, puzzled.

The black-clad figure approached like a phantom. One hand pressed her firmly into his embrace with a force so great it was almost out of control, as if he were trying to knead her into his very bones and blood to confirm this was not a dream that would shatter in an instant.

The young man buried his face in the crook of her neck, breathing in the air that held her scent desperately. His long-suppressed emotions seemed to be wrapped in tremors, and his shoulders and back, usually as cold and hard as iron, were now trembling slightly.

A drop of scalding tear fell unexpectedly, burning the skin on the side of her neck.

Then came a second, a third. The painful, searing sensation seemed to seep into her skin, making her heart ache.

Mu Ran was at a loss.

In her memory, Cang Shubai was mature and steady, yet also very indifferent. Let alone crying, she had never even seen him look sad or distressed.

Although Cang Shubai was not a powerful cultivator, in her heart, she inexplicably felt he was very strong. How could a person with such a strong spirit ever have a day where he would cry?

She thought, this dream she was having was very strange.

Mu Ran subconsciously raised her hand and gently patted his back. Her fingertips touched his snow-white hair, and she couldn't help but tremble slightly.

"Jinzhi, what's wrong?"

He pressed his cheek against hers, his breath scorching, murmuring incessantly, "Don't leave me... Ranran, never leave me."

"I won't leave you," Mu Ran soothed him softly. "Didn't we make a vow when we married? For all eternity, in life and in death, we shall follow one another. You are the person I love; I would never bear to leave you."

The arms wrapped around her body tightened further, like a cage of confinement, as if he wanted to lock her firmly against his chest, never giving her the slightest chance to dissipate.

The body beneath the black fabric was taut and trembling, and the wet, hot breath at her neck grew heavier, mixed with the undried tears, scalding her skin.

Mu Ran felt something wrong under her hand. Her fingers suddenly grabbed his left sleeve—it was empty.

"Where is your arm!" Mu Ran struggled to push away from his embrace, which was so tight it made it hard to breathe. She gripped his sleeve, asking him with mounting agitation, "What happened? You're hurt. Jinzhi, where did your arm go? Can it be found? We can go find a medical cultivator and find a way to reattach it. Jinzhi, stop looking at me like that, say something—"

He kissed her, fierce and cruel.

The collision of their lips was heavy and trembling, carrying the frantic nature of having lost and regained something, and a pain suppressed to the extreme. It was not gentle or lingering; it was a madness bordering on plunder.

He held her body firmly, allowing no room for retreat. His tongue forcefully pried open her teeth, carrying a cool, damp sensation and the salt of undried tears. It entangled with hers, arrogant yet trembling, every friction filled with the despair of fearing she might leave again.

"Don't go, I beg you, don't go."

"That wasn't me... I only have you, I only want you."

"You are my only wife."

Amidst the young man's increasingly uncontrolled murmurs, Mu Ran's breath was plundered by his madness. She felt dizzy and lightheaded, and for the first time, she felt a strange fear toward her own husband.

As the wind blew, ripples formed on the water beneath her feet. In the space where the sea met the sky, the woman's familiar scent vanished.

The white-haired, black-clad youth's arms were empty, just as his heart, which had just resumed beating, became dead silent once more after losing its fullness.

A long, long time later, his figure swayed slightly, and he knelt on the rippling water.

In the reflection of the blue water, that face, usually so cold and isolated, had long since shattered. The corners of his eyes were red, his lips pressed white, and every line on his face was etched with heart-wrenching pain.

His originally black pupils were being swallowed bit by bit by a scarlet hue, turning from deep black to dark crimson, then surging into a fierce, blood-like color.

This was the sign of falling into demonic cultivation.

Mu Ran opened her eyes in a panic, seeing the familiar canopy of her bed. Her breathing was rapid, and she sat up from the bed almost subconsciously. The young man outside happened to walk in at that moment.

"Jinzhi!"

Mu Ran got out of bed and ran into his arms.

Cang Shubai held her and asked, "Did you have a nightmare?"

Mu Ran nodded, her eyes misty.

Cang Shubai naturally picked her up horizontally and sat on the bed, stroking the top of her head. "It was just a nightmare, don't be afraid."

Mu Ran, however, grabbed both of his hands as if still fearful, carefully hugging and touching them, looking at them for a long time.

Cang Shubai had exceptional hearing and had keenly sensed that Mu Ran's breathing was off, which was why he had entered the room.

He had been preparing dinner; his green sleeves were rolled up, revealing his sturdy and well-defined forearms, still damp with water. These hands were perfectly fine; there was nothing wrong with them.

Cang Shubai did not understand what kind of nightmare Mu Ran had had that would make her hold onto his hands and refuse to let go. He was good-natured, though, and let her fiddle with his hands.

Finally, she pressed her palms against his. The girl's hands were soft and slender, the young man's hands large and warm. He closed his fingers, just enough to wrap around her hands completely, as if silently supporting her shaken spirit.

Mu Ran sat on his lap, leaning against his chest. In his familiar scent, she gradually felt a sense of security, and her tense body slowly relaxed.

He asked softly, "Are you feeling better?"

Mu Ran leaned listlessly against his chest, listening to his heartbeat, and slowly nodded.

Cang Shubai's well-defined fingers moved slightly, interlacing with hers one by one. Their hands were clasped, the gaps filled, palms pressed together, as if he were wrapping everything about her within his grasp.

He kissed her brow.

"I am here guarding you, don't be afraid."

chapters.title: Nightmare (Part II)
chapters.content:
Mu Ran’s heart gradually settled, yet the overly vivid nightmare still lingered faintly in her mind. Raising her eyes, she focused intently on his face.

It was different from the one in her dream.

The man before her still had black hair, his skin was not so deathly pale, and there was no suppressed agony between his brows. As he looked at her, his dark eyes curved slightly, holding the same familiar tenderness as always.

Mu Ran called to him softly, “Jinzhi.”

“Mm, I’m here.”

She said, “I had such a strange dream.”

It was a good thing that she was willing to confide in him.

Cang Shubai asked in a low voice, “What kind of dream?”

“In the dream, it felt like I had slept for a very, very long time. After I woke up, I wandered aimlessly for a long time, and then I saw you.” Mu Ran’s brows knitted tightly, and she said with a heavy heart, “But you were so strange in the dream.”

“I was strange?”

She nodded, looking at a lock of black hair on his chest, and said slowly, “Your appearance had changed. Your hair had turned white, and you seemed to have aged so much. And here...”

Mu Ran withdrew her hand, her fingertips lightly touching the space between his brows, and said, “It was as if you were filled with an inseparable sorrow, as if you had suffered so many grievances while I wasn't looking.”

Cang Shubai caught her hand. “What else?”

“And...” Mu Ran looked at his hand, mist filling her eyes and turning into spring rain that spilled from the corners of her eyes. Her voice choked, “This hand of yours was gone.”

She knew it was a dream, but it had felt so real. When she touched the empty sleeve of the man in her dream, she had felt as if the sky were collapsing.

Cang Shubai leaned down and kissed the corner of her eye. “It was just a dream, don’t be afraid.”

Mu Ran reached out to wrap her arms around his neck, burying herself entirely in his embrace.

Cang Shubai gently stroked her back, his voice as soft and low as the evening breeze brushing past one’s ears: “I am here. Both hands are here, perfectly intact, right by your side.”

In this world, there were very few who could make him lose an arm; how could he ever fall into the state she had seen in her dream?

He thought that perhaps the town was becoming unsettled, and his wife was simply too concerned for him, leading to such a terrifying dream.

With Mu Ran, Cang Shubai always possessed boundless patience. Coaxing her into happiness was something he had always done with pleasure and never grew tired of.

“Ranran, perhaps you’ve been too tired these past two days, which is why you had a nightmare. Let’s not take on such late-night work anymore, shall we?”

Mu Ran recalled the miserable state of the old man with the long sword she had seen at Hong Fu’s place, and she couldn't help but wonder if she had been triggered by that bloody scene, leading to such a terrifying dream.

She buried her face in his chest, rubbing against him as she nodded. “Mm, I won’t take such work anymore.”

Mu Ran regained her vitality, lifted her face, and smiled: “I know, a dream is just a dream. Nightmares are the opposite of reality. Jinzhi will definitely be fine. After all, the real Jinzhi wouldn’t be like the one in my dream, who even started crying and shedding tears.”

Cang Shubai was silent for a moment.

She emerged from her lethargic state, braced herself up, and shifted to sit astride his lap to face him better, wrapping her arms around his neck again.

“I smell something fragrant. Is it tofu soup? Are you cooking?”

He nodded and asked, “Are you hungry?”

Mu Ran said, “I’m hungry.”

He chuckled, “Put on your shoes and go wash your hands. It will be ready to eat soon.”

Because Mu Ran had been catching up on sleep and then had the nightmare, their dinner was later than usual. The moon rose with stars for company, and the night did not feel lonely.

She had indeed been tired these past two days; after finishing one bowl of rice, she added half a bowl more, chewing on sweet and sour pork ribs with a ravenous air.

Cang Shubai ladled a bowl of soup for her. “Slow down, no one is going to snatch it from you.”

Mu Ran said indistinctly, “I’ll wash the dishes today.”

She had been lying down for so long, and he had done all the housework by himself; she felt a bit embarrassed.

Cang Shubai said, “We’ll do it together.”

Mu Ran smiled. “Okay.”

When she had eaten her fill, Cang Shubai suddenly asked, “Why didn’t you tell me you were going to the inn today?”

Mu Ran vaguely felt that he was settling scores. “It was because Fairy Hong Fu ordered something. She is a big client, so I delivered it myself. I thought it was just delivering an item and I would be back soon, so I didn’t tell you.”

“I didn’t see you at the Song family workshop, and I was very worried.”

Mu Ran didn't take it to heart. “I’m a grown woman, I won’t get lost. Jinzhi, you’re worrying too much.”

“What if, like last time, you stuck your neck out and encountered danger?”

Mu Ran, who was about to pick up a piece of sweet and sour pork rib, paused, rendered speechless.

Cang Shubai placed a rib into her bowl. “Have you ever thought about what would happen to me if something happened to you?”

Mu Ran felt a sudden surge of guilt. She sat up straight and said obediently, “I’m sorry, Jinzhi. From now on, whenever I go anywhere, I will definitely tell you in advance.”

Cang Shubai lowered his eyes and murmured an “Mm,” then asked, “Did that woman named Hong Fu give you any trouble?”

The world respectfully addressed Hong Fu as a fairy, yet he referred to her as “that woman named Hong Fu,” unwilling to grant even a shred of respect.

It wasn't the first time Mu Ran had felt that her husband occasionally displayed a strange, haughty pride. She shook her head. “She just spoke a few words to me; she didn’t give me any trouble.”

Of course, she omitted the bloody scene she had witnessed and the high-and-mighty attitude of Hong Fu and her companions.

There was no need to say it; saying it would only make Cang Shubai worry. He was just an ordinary doctor at a clinic who could treat injuries and illnesses but could not withstand the cold eyes and slaughter of the immortal sects. There was no need to make him feel distressed.

Mu Ran knew Cang Shubai was sharp. She picked up her bowl and lowered her head to drink soup, using it to avoid his gaze.

They were truly husband and wife, knowing quite a lot about each other.

Cang Shubai said, “Ranran.”

She looked up. “Yes?”

“Would you be willing to accompany me back to my hometown?”

Mu Ran was puzzled. “Back to your hometown?”

“The anniversary of my parents’ passing is coming up. I want to go back to pay my respects, and I also want them to see you.”

Mu Ran knew that Cang Shubai’s parents had both passed away and he had no other relatives. Pitying his loneliness, during the time they had just married, she had wanted to be a considerate, virtuous wife and mother, taking care of everything big and small in the house. However, she didn't know where things had gone wrong later on; instead, she had been spoiled by him and had become increasingly lazy.

Cang Shubai held her hand. “The year we married, I wanted to take you back to my hometown, but I thought the journey was long and there was no need for you to suffer with me. But things are different now.”

How were they different?

He had to maintain a calm expression as he told a lie, “Our life is much better now; we are no longer as strapped for cash as before. I can buy a comfortable carriage so we won’t have to sleep in the open on the road, and you won’t have to endure as much bumping.”

Various factions were gathering in this town. Even though Hong Fu had captured the old man with the long sword, those who coveted the old man’s treasure were still reluctant to leave. A storm would surely rise here sooner or later.

He would not allow this storm to involve her.

Mu Ran did not hesitate. Her eyes curved into crescents as she smiled, “Okay, I’ll go back with you to pay respects to Father and Mother.”

chapters.title: Forbidden Arts
chapters.content:
Since she had decided to leave home for a while, Mu Ran resolved to work harder over the next few days to finish all the little gadgets her customers had previously ordered.

At the Song family workshop that day, she said to Boss Song, "I have to go on a long trip. It should take a month or two. Boss Song, if there are any more orders during this time, they will just have to wait until I return."

Boss Song was very reluctant to let go of such a cash cow as Mu Ran.

Although Mu Ran was not a craftsman belonging to his workshop, her name was associated with his shop, and she had truly brought him a lot of business and earned him a great deal of money.

He couldn't help but ask, "With the end of the year approaching, why are you going on a long trip at this time?"

Mu Ran replied, "I am going back to my hometown with Jinzhi to pay respects to his parents."

Since it was to pay respects to his parents, Boss Song had no reason to try to keep her.

He nodded and said, "Alright. If any more customers come specifically asking for your work, I will explain the situation to them. If they can wait, they can place an order; if they can't, then so be it."

Although Boss Song was a businessman, he was reasonably decent; otherwise, Mu Ran would not have collaborated with him for so long.

Just then, a customer walked into the shop.

Yue Qingfeng wore a blue Taoist robe that outlined his tall, slender frame. His features were refined and handsome, possessing a natural, scholarly grace.

Seeing that he was dressed in the attire of a Chongyang Mountain disciple, Boss Song’s attitude became even more respectful. "Your presence brings light to my humble shop, Daoist. Is there something you need?"

Yue Qingfeng looked straight at Mu Ran and smiled. "I am here to see Miss Mu."

Boss Song looked back and forth between Yue Qingfeng and Mu Ran, muttering to himself. He wondered what kind of luck Mu Ran had recently, that one cultivator after another was coming to find her.

Mu Ran still remembered that this Daoist had stepped in to deal with that violently mutated, half-beast human. She walked over and offered a polite smile. "Is there something you need from me, Daoist?"

Yue Qingfeng said, "That day, I saw Uncle-Master Hongfu use a strange magical artifact to track down the hidden Old Man Changjian. Later, I heard that Uncle-Master Hongfu had commissioned you to make several artifacts called 'paging chickens.' To have gained Uncle-Master Hongfu's favor, I imagine your work must indeed have its merits."

He started with a few compliments before stating the purpose of his visit. "I would like to ask you to help me make a few of the same artifacts. Of course, I will pay exactly what Uncle-Master Hongfu paid. How about it?"

These cultivators from prestigious sects certainly had plenty of money.

Although Mu Ran was tempted by the spirit stones, she shook her head and said truthfully, "I am going back to my hometown with my husband and will be away for a long time. If you can wait two months, Daoist, I could take the order."

She guessed that cultivators were all very busy and that Yue Qingfeng probably wouldn't have that much time to wait, but Yue Qingfeng's answer exceeded her expectations.

"In that case, I will come back to collect them in two months."

Mu Ran was stunned for a moment, then quickly said, "Alright."

At the medical clinic, after sending off a patient, Dr. Hu bowed and scraped as he served tea and water to his godfather.

Cang Shubai sat in a chair, flipping through a book in his hand. Without looking up, he said, "I need to leave for a while. During this time, you will continue to stay here as the clinic's doctor. If there is any movement, send me a message."

Dr. Hu was deeply surprised. "Why is Godfather leaving? Is your cultivation about to break through a bottleneck?"

Cang Shubai did indeed feel that his cultivation realm was about to have a breakthrough soon, and he needed a safe environment to advance. But the more important reason was, "There will soon be a storm of blood and chaos here, and I don't want Ranran to be implicated in this turmoil."

So, it was for his godmother again.

Dr. Hu glanced at Cang Shubai gloomily. He felt that the more "human" this malevolent star seemed, the more awkward it made him feel. When he first encountered Cang Shubai, Cang Shubai was merely a Foundation Establishment cultivator.

But Cang Shubai was insidious; not only did he kill people above his rank, but he also slaughtered the small sect he had originally joined. That bloodthirsty appearance had even caused Dr. Hu, who had tried to fish for treasures in the chaos, to fall into his hands.

Later, a restriction was placed on Dr. Hu's heart; if Cang Shubai died, Dr. Hu would die as well.

Dr. Hu had no choice but to obey Cang Shubai in everything. At first, he was full of resentment, waiting for an opportunity to break the restriction and kill Cang Shubai in return. But having been by Cang Shubai's side for so many years, he had indeed gained many benefits, and his desire to kill Cang Shubai had become much more nuanced.

Cang Shubai was taking his beautiful wife back to his hometown, leaving him here to work like a beast of burden.

Dr. Hu was slightly dissatisfied but dared not show it. He glanced at the book in Cang Shubai's hand and asked strangely, "Godfather, are you interested in forbidden arts again?"

Forbidden arts were called forbidden because they required a price to be paid by the user.

Cultivators loved to scheme against others to snatch resources, but it was rare to see someone wanting to learn forbidden arts that would harm themselves.

Cang Shubai did not answer Dr. Hu. This book recording forbidden arts was something he had scavenged over two hundred years ago when he slaughtered the first small sect he belonged to.

At the time, he hadn't been interested in so-called forbidden arts; it was only because of the dream Mu Ran had mentioned that he had felt a whim to dig it out.

As he turned another page of the book, his fingertips paused slightly.

—Sever a meridian in one's own body, using one's own essence, blood, and bone marrow as a guide, transforming one's life-force into a binding to entangle a soul that is scattering and drifting away.

Sever an inch, bind a fraction; the more intense the agony of the cracking bones, the slower the soul's drift, until the strand of soul about to dissipate is firmly locked within one's own shell by one's own blood and bone, never to dissipate again.

Cang Shubai frowned, a sense of inexplicable gloom settling over him.

Dr. Hu felt that something was wrong and retreated silently, not daring to make a sound.

As usual, before the sun had set, Cang Shubai arrived at the entrance of the workshop to pick her up.

Mu Ran ran out with light steps, looking up with a bright smile. "Jinzhi, I took another big order today."

Cang Shubai took her hand and walked back, saying softly, "Didn't you say you wouldn't take any more orders?"

"Yes, that's what I said, but Daoist Yue said he could wait two months to pick them up. There's no rush, I can take my time making them, so I agreed."

He asked, "Daoist Yue?"

"The one who stepped forward to resolve the crisis that day when the half-beast human mutated and tried to hurt people. We exchanged names; he is called Yue Qingfeng, a thirteenth-generation disciple of Chongyang Mountain." Mu Ran’s expression was filled with admiration. "Chongyang Mountain... I've heard of this sect before. It is said that they all practice the sword path. Unlike other sects that would easily wipe out another sect just to plunder resources, their sect motto is just the word 'Righteousness'."

chapters.title: Coming and Going Like the Wind
chapters.content:
Mu Ran sighed again, "Interacting with Daoist Yue today, he truly lives up to his reputation. He is gentle, courteous, and possesses a righteous and open character."

Cang Shubai listened to her prattling on about how wonderful the disciples of Chongyang Mountain were, and let out an ambiguous "Hmm." "Then should we chase after him and ask for his contact information?"

"That won't be necessary. He'll be coming back to the workshop in two months anyway."

"I thought that if you exchanged contact information with him, you might be able to better appreciate his gentleness, courtesy, and righteous, open character."

Mu Ran realized it only then. She raised her head and looked closely at her husband’s cold, indifferent face.

He looked much the same as usual, always wearing that aloof expression, but his pitch-black eyes held a deep, lingering gaze that allowed her—the person closest to him—to detect a different flavor.

"Hmm, that is indeed true." Mu Ran nodded as if it were a serious matter, then quickly hugged his arm and smiled. "But I still prefer someone who is calm and composed, who saves lives and heals the wounded, and who smells like medicinal herbs."

Cang Shubai automatically ignored the "saves lives and heals the wounded" part, which didn't fit him at all. Being watched by her smiling eyes, the space between his brows couldn't help but soften, and a hint of a smile appeared at the corners of his slightly upturned lips.

Mu Ran pretended to sniff him exaggeratedly. "There’s a sour smell."

He asked calmly, "Is there?"

She nodded. "There is."

Cang Shubai said, "If there’s an unpleasant smell, then I must be quite annoying."

Mu Ran laughed out loud. "Not at all, I like it!"

Cang Shubai leaned down slightly and, as if rewarding her, fed her another sugar pill.

Mu Ran obediently held it in her mouth, feeling the sweetness spread, and mumbled, "Jinzhi, are these really just ordinary sugar pills you bought?"

"Why do you ask?"

His fingertips gently brushed the corner of her lips. The touch was soft, and he felt a sudden urge to kiss her, but since they were out in public, he had to let it go.

Mu Ran said, "Every time I finish a sugar pill, I feel particularly comfortable, as if I have endless energy. These days, when I go to the entrance of the village to listen to gossip, Auntie Wang and the others all say my complexion is getting more and more rosy."

Cang Shubai held her hand and continued walking forward, saying in an emotionless tone, "The person who makes the sugar said that medicinal herbs for strengthening the body were added to the pills."

Mu Ran: "Ah?"

"Don't worry, I am a doctor. These medicines are very common and have no ill effects on your body."

Mu Ran pressed further, "Then you must have spent a lot of money. Is your pocket money still enough? If others invite you out for meals or social engagements, you won't be mocked for being short on cash, will you?"

Cang Shubai felt quite helpless. He looked down at Mu Ran's worried face, and his heart felt a warmth rising. His fingertips lightly pinched the flesh on her cheek. "Who would dare to mock me?"

Mu Ran thought to herself, there are plenty of people in this world who would dare to mock you.

Out of consideration for his pride, she decided she should increase his pocket money when they got back. After all, their life was much better now, and there was no need for him to keep suffering.

As the sun set, the forest path was shrouded in dim, yellow light. The forest ahead trembled faintly, and the birds were silent. The overly quiet atmosphere added a touch of eeriness.

Cang Shubai suddenly grabbed Mu Ran's hand and blocked her path.

At the same time, a man with a twisted physique lunged out.

His eyes were bloodshot, and the skin and flesh all over his body were cracking inch by inch. Dark red beads of blood oozed out from the cracks, and beneath the fissures, eerie crimson patterns suddenly emerged, winding and writhing under his skin like living creatures.

Mu Ran poked her head out from behind Cang Shubai. Seeing the strange person before her, she clutched Cang Shubai's sleeve tightly. "It's a person who has been corrupted by a demonic beast, just like last time."

"Blood... I need blood... I need a lot... a lot of blood..."

The eyeballs in his sockets were almost popping out as he stared fixedly at the young man and woman on the path, his craving for blood seemingly overflowing from his broken body.

Mu Ran thought that her husband was just a frail doctor and likely couldn't withstand a single blow from this demonic creature. She reached into her storage pouch to pull out the life-saving talisman she had bought at a high price. Before she could act, the creature charged over with incredible speed.

Cang Shubai’s eyes flashed with a faint, icy blue light. He had captured the movement hidden in the wind a step earlier. He lowered his eyes slightly, raised his hand to pull Mu Ran into his arms, and left his completely unguarded back to the creature.

Just as the creature's claws struck, about to tear Cang Shubai's back to shreds, a sword light pierced through the air, cleanly severing the creature's arm.

Yue Qingfeng arrived on his flying sword. "Monster, die!"

Yue Qingfeng stepped on his sword, his figure swooping down like a startled swan. His long, blue-edged sword wove a sharp web of sword flowers, and a cold light slashed down.

The blade grazed the creature's side, drawing blood. As he spun, the sword's momentum deepened, piercing straight into the creature's glabella. After a shrill scream, the creature stood frozen on the spot. A bloody hole appeared in its forehead, and the crimson patterns all over its body instantly dimmed and dissipated before it collapsed with a crash.

As the creature fell into a pool of blood, spider lilies suddenly sprouted from the crimson stains. The bewitching petals grew wildly, wrapping around the body and swallowing the remains in an instant, leaving only a field of eerie red floral shadows.

Mu Ran grabbed the arm the young man had used to shield her head and stood on tiptoe in his embrace, her eyes full of joy. "Daoist Yue!"

Yue Qingfeng sheathed his sword and walked over. "Are you two alright?"

Mu Ran shook her head. "It's a good thing you arrived in time, otherwise my husband and I might have been torn to pieces."

Cang Shubai lowered his hand and stood guard beside Mu Ran, silent and unmoving.

Like Mu Ran, he possessed no talent for cultivation.

Yue Qingfeng withdrew his scrutinizing gaze and said, "I heard recently that a demonic creature was harming people, and I have been tracking its trail. I didn't expect to run into you here; it is truly fate."

Mu Ran returned the favor. "Thank you, Daoist, for your help. How about this—I won't charge you for the items you ordered from me."

Yue Qingfeng laughed. "That won't do. Business is business. Even if it hadn't been you two I encountered today, I would still have stepped in to help. You are a craftsperson who earns a living with your skills; I cannot let you work for free."

Mu Ran said admiringly, "The Daoist is truly noble and upright. So open and honorable—you are worthy of being a gentleman from Chongyang Mountain."

Yue Qingfeng cupped his hands. "Demonic creatures have been appearing frequently lately, and it is getting late. You two should return home early. I have other matters to attend to, so I will take my leave."

He swept his long sword, and the spider lilies blooming in the blood and the remains on the ground turned to dust and vanished. He nodded in farewell once more and flew away on his sword.

Mu Ran watched his back as he flew through the air. "Coming and going like the wind—truly dashing."

Suddenly, a cold wind rose.

The sword beneath Yue Qingfeng's feet suddenly lost its balance. His body tilted, and he plummeted like a falling star, disappearing along with his sword into the distance.

Cang Shubai said, "Indeed, coming and going like the wind."

Mu Ran: "..."

chapters.title: Falling Snow
chapters.content:
"Yue Qingfeng, a thirteenth-generation disciple of Chongyang Mountain, apprentice to Master Yuwei, and a direct disciple of the Chongyang Mountain ancestor. He possesses excellent talent and is highly regarded. The Chongyang Mountain ancestor has been in seclusion for over five hundred years, during which time Master Yuwei has managed the sect's affairs. It seems to be the unspoken consensus on Chongyang Mountain that Yue Qingfeng will be the next sect leader."

Cang Shubai sat by the window, staring at the information recorded on the paper in his hand, remaining silent for a long moment.

Not long ago, Dr. Hu had specifically gathered this intelligence and used a talisman to quickly deliver it to Cang Shubai. However, as it was a rushed investigation into Yue Qingfeng, this was all the information that could be uncovered for now.

The monster's attack had been sudden, yet Yue Qingfeng's appearance had been perfectly timed.

Was this truly just a coincidence?

Suddenly hearing a gasp from inside the room, Cang Shubai let the paper in his hand vanish into flames. At the same time, his figure appeared in the room in the blink of an eye, catching the person who had fallen from the chair.

Mu Ran landed in his steady, familiar embrace and looked up with a smile, "Jinzhi, you arrived just in time."

Cang Shubai helped her down from the chair and asked, "What were you doing?"

Mu Ran patted the small box in her hands, "Aren't we going on a long journey? I need to bring these things along."

These were life-saving items she had bought after saving money for the past few years—talismans and magical artifacts. They were not cheap, though in Cang Shubai's eyes, they were of little use. Consequently, he had quietly replaced many of the things she bought; she had no idea that the small box she was clutching contained items that would make many cultivators green with envy.

Mu Ran was truly precious of her life. It was as if she had experienced the cruelty of the cultivation world, making her exceptionally cautious and prepared. After the frequent nightmares she had been having lately, she even felt that the life-saving items she had bought were not enough.

Cang Shubai took the items from her hands, "Let me handle such things."

Mu Ran replied, "I can manage these small tasks. Besides, I can't rely on you for everything."

"Why not?"

Mu Ran: "Huh?"

Cang Shubai held her hand, "I am your husband; it is only right that you rely on me."

Mu Ran looked at his tall back and let out an "oh."

Sometimes, she felt that her husband, who appeared cold and aloof, was actually quite overbearing. At the very least, when he held her hand like this, it didn't look like he was using much strength, but no matter what, she could never pull her hand away from his.

Snow was falling tonight. Pushing open the window, one could see the snowflakes drifting down. A basin of charcoal fire was lit in the room; at such a time, admiring the snow from a warm room was a fine choice.

The bamboo couch by the window was covered with a plain, soft mattress. He sat her down on the couch and leaned in beside her, his fingertips still hooked around hers. The bamboo couch creaked slightly, adding a touch of lingering tenderness.

Mu Ran couldn't sit still. She crawled to the window and reached a hand out, catching a snowflake. Soon, it melted into a droplet of water in her palm.

She found it interesting, but a tall frame soon pressed down behind her. She was firmly enclosed between the window sill and his chest, unable to move.

The young man's large hand gently but firmly pulled her hand back from outside the window, holding her hand, which had been chilled by the cold wind, and slowly warming it in his palm.

"Your constitution is weak; be careful not to catch a cold."

Mu Ran pursed her lips in slight boredom, habitually relaxing her body to lean back against his chest, muttering, "I feel like my body has become much stronger after taking those sugar pills."

It was just playing with a few snowflakes; she didn't think she was so fragile that she would catch a cold.

Cang Shubai said, "Don't make me worry."

"Alright, alright, I know." Mu Ran leaned obediently in his arms, lazily staring at the swirling snowflakes outside, and truly stopped moving.

Cang Shubai let out a low chuckle and pulled her closer, his chin resting gently on the top of her head. His warm breath, mixed with the cold scent of snow from outside the window, fell against her temples.

He raised his hand to tuck her collar in, his fingertips inadvertently brushing against her slightly cool cheek. His voice was soft and gentle: "It is better to be this obedient."

Mu Ran was someone who was somewhat free-spirited.

For instance, on that rainy night more than two years ago, she was soaked through and alone, yet she dared to knock on a man's door.

Not long after they were married, Cang Shubai had asked her, "Weren't you afraid that I was a lecher and would harbor evil intentions toward you?"

At that time, Mu Ran had laughed happily, "You wouldn't be a lecher. When we were neighbors, I often brushed past you, and I never saw you look at me even once!"

Cang Shubai thought that his wife was indeed not very clever.

She had never realized that he never interacted with others; how could that rainy night have been an exception for him to open the door and help her repair her leaking roof?

If he hadn't harbored ulterior motives long ago, how could he and she have walked through every step so perfectly, to the point where they were now a loving couple in the eyes of outsiders?

He was not as noble and upright as she imagined; he was merely an ordinary man capable of desire.

Later on, he discovered that her life was also very casual.

She had no routine for her three daily meals. If she didn't feel hungry, she could just gnaw on a single steamed bun for the entire day. Sometimes, if she saw a shooting star at night, she would run outside wearing thin clothes, not afraid of freezing herself. Staying up late to tinker with her little gadgets was also a common occurrence.

But fortunately, she had some self-awareness and knew her lifestyle was truly poor, so she obediently listened to his discipline. This was perhaps the part that made Cang Shubai feel at ease.

Tonight, the falling snow was perfect for two people to huddle together for warmth.

Cang Shubai lowered his eyes, noticing that Mu Ran's gaze was still fixed on the swirling snowflakes.

In this remote town, winter snow was not uncommon.

However, in those sects and mountain peaks rich in spiritual energy, suitable for cultivation, snow was a rare sight.

Cang Shubai reached out, caught a few snowflakes, and brought them before her eyes.

Mu Ran looked up in pleasant surprise.

Cang Shubai said softly, "I don't fear the cold. If you want to watch, watch to your heart's content."

The emotions in his heart were quite subtle. He cultivated an extremely cold technique and was naturally cold-hearted and indifferent, his joy and anger supposed to be as calm as a stagnant pool. Let alone a snowfall, even turning a ten-mile radius into a frozen wasteland would be effortless for him. Yet now, to please his wife, he was cupping a few snowflakes as if he were offering a precious treasure.

Mu Ran turned around, her beautiful eyes sparkling, "Jinzhi, you are so kind."

Cang Shubai suddenly felt that perhaps doing something like cupping snow for her was not a bad thing to do more often.

Mu Ran, however, picked up a handkerchief and wiped his hands clean.

He asked, "Not watching anymore?"

Mu Ran said, "Snow falls every year; it's no big deal if I miss a little. But if your hands get frostbitten, my heart will ache."

chapters.title: Chapter 24 Will It Slap You in the Face
chapters.content:
Cang Shubai caught her hand and placed a light kiss on her fingertips.

Mu Rang smiled. "Are you going back to town tomorrow?"

He nodded. "I asked Doctor Hu to help pick a carriage. Tomorrow, I'll go pay for it and bring it back."

"Then take me with you," Mu Rang said. "We definitely won't be back for New Year's. Aunt Wang and the others have taken good care of me, so I want to buy some gifts for them."

Cang Shubai replied, "Alright."

"We'll be traveling far, so we need to prepare enough dry rations. In case we don't come across any post stations along the way, we won't go hungry."

"Also, we should bring some low-grade spirit stones. If we run into bandits, we can hand them over to ensure our safety."

"And, the wind is harsh on the road. I packed two extra cold-resistant clothes for you, with the cuffs sewn tight."

"Jin... do your parents like anything? This time we're going to pay our respects to them, so we should buy something they like..."

She leaned against his chest, chattering on without pause, unaware that the usually cold and distant gaze of the man beside her—like a frozen abyss—had been warmed by her trivial yet sincere words, now carrying the soft glow of candlelight.

By midnight, the snow had stopped, so there wasn't much accumulation the next morning. However, a light drizzle fell, and the wind was even colder.

Strangely, when Cang Shubai held the newly bought oil-paper umbrella over Mu Rang's head, the biting cold vanished without a trace.

Mu Rang looked up at the ordinary oil-paper umbrella and said doubtfully, "Jin... did you spend a fortune again on something enchanted?"

Cang Shubai didn't answer. He simply held her hand and said, "The agreed payment time is near. We should hurry."

Mu Rang was now certain—he had definitely spent a lot of money in secret again.

When they arrived in town, the atmosphere was inexplicably tense. Cultivators were everywhere, their eyes scanning about as if each had their own schemes.

Cang Shubai took Mu Rang to the medical hall.

Doctor Hu almost blurted out "Dad," but seeing Cang Shubai's cold expression and then noticing Mu Rang beside him, he swallowed the words. He cleared his throat and put on the demeanor of a shopkeeper.

"Ah, Xiao Cang, you're here so late today. I thought you didn't want the carriage anymore."

Cang Shubai took out a money pouch. "Thank you for your trouble, Doctor Hu. Please accept this as a token of appreciation."

Doctor Hu took the money without hesitation and secretly sent a voice transmission to Cang Shubai. "Old Man Longjian escaped. Now, all the cultivators in town want to find him to claim his treasures for themselves. Red Fu had imprisoned Longjian before, and everyone was eyeing him, but they didn't dare act because of her high cultivation. But now, it's said that Longjian escaped with the help of a demonic cultivator, and Red Fu was injured. Her influence isn't what it used to be."

As he spoke, Doctor Hu felt a stir of ambition in his own heart.

No wonder Red Fu had tortured Longjian for so long without him revealing where the treasure was—turns out he had been certain someone would come to rescue him all along.

Now that Red Fu was weakened, Doctor Hu also wanted a share.

"If you recklessly rush into danger, I won't help you."

Doctor Hu's mind jolted, and he looked up.

Cang Shubai was lowering his gaze, picking up a small piece of licorice root, and feeding it to Mu Rang like she was a hamster. She had been curiously examining the medicinal herbs.

The licorice root was sweet.

Mu Rang covered her mouth, disapprovingly glaring at Cang Shubai before cautiously glancing at Doctor Hu.

She was afraid Doctor Hu would get angry—how dare a mere worker like Cang Shubai feed her shop herbs like snacks?

Doctor Hu could only look around aimlessly, pretending he saw nothing.

Cang Shubai chuckled softly. "Let's go. We'll buy the gifts you want to give."

Mu Rang nodded and quickly pulled Cang Shubai out of the medical hall.

Cang Shubai opened the oil-paper umbrella, placing one hand on Mu Rang's shoulder, considerately shielding her at his side. The umbrella always tilted toward her, giving the biting wind no chance to reach her.

Doctor Hu clicked his tongue twice, mimicking someone's words from before with a sarcastic tone. "I married her only to break through my cultivation. After a hundred years, when she dies of old age, I will return to the immortal path. We will have nothing to do with each other."

He then exaggerated his expression. "Dies of old age, returns to the immortal path, nothing to do with each other—his soul is already taken, will it slap him in the face or not!"

Doctor Hu only dared to grumble behind their backs. Then he remembered Cang Shubai's warning and shivered, deciding to abandon the idea of joining the others in hunting for treasure.

Mu Rang had earned a lot of money these past few days and decided to splurge by taking Cang Shubai out for a good meal.

The restaurant was bustling with people.

A group of cultivators walked together, still discussing Longjian.

"With so many factions gathering, we're outnumbered. This time, we might be at a disadvantage."

"Isn't there a Cang Shu branch family nearby? Use the bloodline command to summon them to help."

"As long as we promise them some benefits, they'll definitely rush to join."

"Right. Being able to help the main family is a rare honor for the branch family. Third Young Master, the family head specifically sent you out to find Longjian's whereabouts, so he must want to temper you. If you handle this well, won't the Cang Shu family's resources be yours to claim over your brothers?"

These cultivators wore matching attire, and the most noble among them was a young man named Cang Shu Haoxue.

Cang Shu Haoxue had been reluctant to come to this backwater town in the first place. Since Red Fu had already captured Longjian first, he hadn't dared to compete with her. Now that Longjian had escaped and Red Fu was injured, he should indeed seize this opportunity.

If he returned to the Cang Shu family with the treasure Longjian had taken from the Void Secret Realm two hundred years ago, his father and the clan elders would surely regard him differently. The position of the next family head—wouldn't it naturally fall to him?

Cang Shu Haoxue took out a jade command token with a blood-red vein pattern. Any member of the Cang Shu bloodline within a hundred-mile radius would sense the command and come to pay their respects.

As he passed by the entrance, Cang Shu Haoxue couldn't help but look up.

A man in blue robes closed his oil-paper umbrella, revealing the face of the woman at his side.

Her brows and eyes were gentle, her skin as white as snow.

Cang Shu Haoxue had initially taken her for an ordinary woman, but he hadn't expected to find such a beautiful girl in this backwater town. As she walked by, it seemed as if a fragrant breeze followed her.

Someone called out, "Third Young Master?"

Cang Shu Haoxue snapped back to reality, regretfully clicking his tongue. "If only she were a female cultivator. Dual cultivation with her would be greatly beneficial. Even if she isn't a cultivator, if she's still a virgin, it would still be... interesting."

The others knew their young master's lustful nature, but Cang Shu Haoxue had a "purity complex"—he disdained women who had been with other men.

"Third Young Master, once we return, what kind of female cultivator can't you get?"

"Yeah, this woman is just an ordinary village wife. How can she compare to the women of Mount Yue City?"

"Once you become the family head, even women like Red Fu will be lining up to fawn over you. Let alone an ordinary village woman like her."

Cang Shu Haoxue felt they were right. He shook the jade token in his hand. "Fine. Let those useless branch family members do the work for us. They can be our cannon fodder."

Mu Rang settled into a private room, pondering what dishes to order.

Cang Shubai poured her a cup of hot tea. "I left something at the medical hall. Mu Mu, I'll go back and get it."

Mu Rang didn't even look up. "Got it. I'll wait for you here."

chapters.title: Cangshu Ran
chapters.content:
When Cangshu Haoxue left Zhenyue Mountain City this time, he had specifically promised the clan elders that he would absolutely return with the old man Changjian’s treasure.

Later, when Hong Fu appeared halfway, Cangshu Haoxue thought he might be able to use his status as the Third Young Master of Zhenyue Mountain City to ask for a favor from her, settling for a few ordinary treasures to take back and fulfill his mission.

But Hong Fu was arrogant and wouldn't even agree to see him.

Now that Hong Fu was injured and the old man Changjian had escaped, wasn't this the perfect opportunity?

Cangshu Haoxue led his few lackeys away from the crowd and into a quiet bamboo forest. He couldn't call for help with too much fanfare, or it would alert others and make things difficult.

Under the expectant gazes of his followers, Cangshu Haoxue took out a jade tablet.

This tablet was a life-saving tool given to him by his father before he left home. With this tablet, any member of the Cangshu branch families had to come to his aid unconditionally. If they refused, they could wait for the main family to cut off all resources and watch themselves slowly degenerate into commoners.

Cangshu Haoxue activated the blood-colored patterns within the jade tablet. As the translucent tablet began to emit a faint glow, he said, "People of the Cangshu family, come forth and pay your respects."

The wind stirred, the bamboo shadows danced, but there was no sign of anyone, nor was there any response.

One of his lackeys asked curiously, "What is going on?"

Another said, "Could it be that the branch family members actually dare to disobey the main family’s command?"

Someone else added, "Unless they’ve gone mad, don't they know the consequences of offending the main family?"

Cangshu Haoxue said impatiently, "Shut up!"

The others immediately fell silent, terrified.

Refusing to believe it, Cangshu Haoxue activated the blood-colored patterns on the jade tablet once more. This time, the patterns responded with a fluctuation; someone with the Cangshu bloodline had arrived.

Sure enough, a figure slowly appeared.

Rain streaks slanted across the bamboo sea, dampening his black hair. His green robes were clean, and his gait was light and slow, like a breeze emerging from the mountain mist.

The man who appeared had a plain, unremarkable face—so ordinary that it was entirely forgettable, as if one would forget this unremarkable appearance the moment they blinked.

Cangshu Haoxue glanced at the jade tablet in his hand and said, "You are from the Cangshu branch family."

The plain-looking man in green robes bowed and said with refined courtesy, "Indeed. I am Cangshu Ran from the Song City branch family."

Cangshu Haoxue didn't care what some small fry from a branch family was called, nor did he deign to remember the name of a minor character. He swept a glance over the plain man again; he was merely at the Foundation Establishment stage, useless for any major task.

Cangshu Haoxue stood with his hands behind his back, his demeanor arrogant. "Why did only you come from the branch family? Where are the others?"

Cangshu Ran replied, "Half a month ago, the Cangshu family in Song City was attacked by madmen, resulting in heavy casualties. The Patriarch is currently tending to the wounded in the manor. Having received the summons of the bloodline command, the Patriarch dared not be negligent and specifically ordered me to explain the situation to you, Young Master. I hope you will not take offense."

Cangshu Haoxue frowned. "Someone actually dared to touch the Cangshu family? Who is bold enough to do that?"

"The madmen were cunning and have left no trace. The Patriarch suspects they came for the branch family's supreme treasure, the Hongmeng Glazed Lamp."

Every family had some hidden treasures at the bottom of their chests. Even if the Cangshu family in Song City was just a branch, they would have one or two treasures that others envied.

"A branch family is just a branch family; truly low-class things." Cangshu Haoxue had no intention of helping the branch family seek justice. He couldn't be bothered with meddling and turned to leave.

Cangshu Ran added, "The Patriarch has a premonition that he cannot protect the treasure and fears it will fall into the hands of outsiders. Upon learning that someone from the main family had arrived, he was overjoyed. He wishes to entrust the treasure to you, Young Master, to take back to the main family, and hopes you will put in a good word for us. Given that the branch family is loyal to the main family, he begs the main family Patriarch to bestow a few sacred healing pills."

Cangshu Haoxue’s heart stirred.

The man beside him whispered, "Third Young Master, the Hongmeng Glazed Lamp is a great item that can help people break through. If this thing were in your hands, it would surely be put to even greater use."

Cangshu Haoxue had just thought of that himself. Even if he couldn't bring back the old man Changjian’s treasure, bringing back the Hongmeng Glazed Lamp to fulfill his mission wouldn't be bad.

Cangshu Haoxue said coldly, "Cangshu Ran, is it? Lead the way."

Cangshu Ran turned his back and walked slowly forward.

The group followed behind him, still desperately flattering Cangshu Haoxue.

"Once we return to Zhenyue Mountain City, Third Young Master will surely have the greatest credit. Not only the disciples of the sect, but even the Patriarch and the elders will look at you with new eyes."

"That's right. So what if the First Young Master is called a rare genius of the century? He is a loner who doesn't associate with anyone in the sect; no one respects him."

"And the Second Young Master, his background... tsk, that goes without saying."

"The Fourth Young Master is still young and is just a fool."

"Only the Third Young Master has a clear mind and handles things thoroughly. Returning to the city this time, you are surely the hope of everyone. In the future, when it comes to ruling Zhenyue Mountain City, only the Third Young Master is truly suitable."

Everyone chimed in, their sycophantic words flowing endlessly. Cangshu Haoxue listened with joy in his heart, as if the high seat of Zhenyue Mountain City had already been prepared for him in advance.

Cangshu Haoxue lifted his chin and said, "When I sit on the position of Patriarch, I will first take down Chiyan Peak and make Hong Fu my warm-bed concubine. Then, Biyun Mountain—I hear there are many beauties there. It’s a pity the most beautiful one married into the Wuyu Palace."

Someone replied, "I actually heard that a young lady from Biyun Mountain had her name struck from the genealogy and was driven off the mountain. Her whereabouts are still unknown."

"Really?" Cangshu Haoxue’s eyes lit up. "I wonder how her beauty compares to the young lady we saw at the restaurant today? If she is even a fraction more beautiful, I wouldn't mind taking in this homeless young lady."

The back leading the way suddenly stopped.

Someone asked, "Hey, why did you—"

Before the words could finish, his head tilted and fell from his neck, landing in the dirt.

The others took a moment to react, then were instantly struck with horror.

"What is going on?"

"There's a trap here!"

"It's a formation!"

The last word was still stuck in his throat when the entire bamboo forest, the moment they stepped into the death gate, erupted with a danger that chilled them to the bone.

Invisible restrictions were fully activated beneath their feet. Pale green spiritual light snaked around everyone's ankles like vipers, and fine bamboo spikes burst from the ground, instantly piercing through their soles.

Immediately, screams rose one after another.

Someone tried to circulate their spiritual power to break free, only to find that the spiritual energy of heaven and earth around them had long been swallowed by the formation, and the true essence within their bodies was like a clay ox entering the sea—they couldn't gather even a bit of it.

chapters.title: Have a Sip of Warm Tea
chapters.content:
Even more terrifying was that those seemingly ordinary green bamboos had now transformed into living creatures. The bamboo joints grew frantically, and sharp branches, like blades, lashed out to strangle, slicing the two closest men in half at the waist in an instant.

Warm beads of blood slid down the bamboo leaves, sending ripples across the stagnant water.

Cangshu Haoxue was already scared out of his wits. He stumbled backward, his fingertips tapping frantically on his storage ring, desperate to crush the protective jade talisman he kept as a last resort. However, the very moment the talisman’s spiritual light was about to ignite, a figure closed in like a ghost.

The man in green held no blade; his fingertips contained only condensed, pure killing intent. He brushed them lightly across Cangshu Haoxue’s neck, and with a soft *puchi* sound, it was as if he were slicing through a piece of rotting meat.

Cangshu Haoxue’s head soared into the sky, his face still frozen in an expression of shock, but the moment his eyes landed, they met the man in green’s eyes—eyes as still as an ancient well.

There was no emotion in them, not even a trace of killing intent, only an indifference capable of freezing a soul.

A sharp chill pierced through tendons and shattered bones. A bloody mist mixed with the light rain instantly permeated the air. The disciple who had been full of flattery just moments ago, and the young master who had been so sought after, were reduced to scattered remains and bloody mud in the blink of an eye, with not even a complete corpse left to be found.

The ice-blue little fish, catching the scent of blood, happily crawled out from the youth’s sleeve. It swam joyfully through the air thick with the stench of death, devouring one soul after another that had died in agony.

It was great to follow its master; there was a feast every few days.

Suddenly, however, it heard a "crunch."

The cold fish stared over, just in time to see the youth retract his foot.

The headless corpse on the ground had its lower half crushed into a bloody mess by that single step.

Watching its master’s back, the cold fish couldn't help but shiver.

The man in green moved his fingers slightly, and a plain oil-paper umbrella slowly emerged from his palm. He lifted his wrist, and as the umbrella surface flickered, the ordinary paper shed its mundane appearance in an instant, returning to its true form.

The ribs of the umbrella were as translucent and white as jade, and upon its surface bloomed flowers of red plum, so vivid they looked as if they had been soaked in fresh blood.

A faint, freezing mist spread with the wind of the umbrella. Wherever it passed, blood droplets instantly froze, and the scattered remains on the ground were covered inch by inch in a thin frost, with delicate ice patterns forming on the flesh.

The Red Plum White Jade Umbrella—everyone in the world knew this was the "Old Man Longjian's" life-saving treasure.

And who could say that the tragic state of these frozen corpses was not the work of the Red Plum White Jade Umbrella?

The blue cold fish shivered again.

Truly, this was not the first time it had felt its master was quite sinister.

The jade-like umbrella returned to the appearance of a plain, unremarkable oil-paper umbrella. A talisman appeared in the youth’s hand and burned to ashes.

His face, now exposed to the cool, misty rain, looked increasingly sharp and refined. His brows were slanted like a blade, the corners of his eyes slightly upturned, and his pupils were as deep as a cold pool. His originally plain features now seemed as if they had been meticulously carved, possessing a cold, clear elegance.

He opened the umbrella to shield himself from the wind and snow. As he turned, the hem of his green robes fluttered, yet not a single speck of blood or dust touched them.

"Let's go back."

The cold fish took one last look at the corpses on the ground, let out a satisfied burp, and swam through the air, obediently returning to its master’s sleeve.

Far away in the city of Zhenyue Mountain, a lamp flickered twice in the wind and suddenly went out.

The lamp-keeper turned deathly pale, stumbling toward the lamp. His fingers trembled as he touched the cold base, and he ran out screaming.

"Disaster! The Third Young Master’s life lamp has gone out!"

In the restaurant, the noise was constant.

Mu Ran rested her chin in her hands, looking toward the entrance of the private room several times.

Finally, after the umpteenth time she looked, the person she was waiting for returned.

Cangshu Bai walked in slowly, his green robes still carrying a lingering chill. The cold, unapproachable aura around him seemed to meet warm light and silently dissolve the moment he caught sight of her bright, joyful eyes.

"Sorry, I’m late."

Mu Ran took his hand and pulled him to sit down. Holding his slightly cold hands, she asked, "Why were you gone for so long?"

Cangshu Bai replied, "A patient arrived at the clinic unexpectedly. Doctor Hu was overwhelmed, so he asked me to help him treat the patient."

Mu Ran complained a little, "But today is your day off. Doctor Hu still made you work without even paying you."

Cangshu Bai said, "Then I won't help next time."

Mu Ran thought for a moment, then shook her head. "But if a patient comes, there’s nothing you can do. Your work is about saving lives, unlike my tinkering with tools; you can’t just stop when you want to."

Cangshu Bai gave a soft "Hmm" and placed a pastry on the table. "I saw freshly baked osmanthus cakes on my way back, so I bought some."

Mu Ran touched it; it was still warm. She leaned a little closer to him, lifted her face, and smiled. "I suppose you’re thoughtful enough. I won’t blame you for being out so long this time."

Cangshu Bai’s large hand was still being held by her small ones. The warm, delicate sensation of the girl’s skin against his fingertips dispelled the last traces of the cold rain that had clung to him, leaving not a shadow behind.

Mu Ran asked him, "You must be hungry, right?"

Cangshu Bai nodded. "I am."

She called out toward the door, "Waiter, order!"

The waiter running the floor quickly pushed the door open and walked in. "What would the two guests like to order?"

Mu Ran didn't hesitate, crisply reciting the dishes, "Clear bamboo fungus soup, braised venison with sauce, stir-fried mushrooms with fresh bamboo shoots, and a portion of honey-glazed water chestnuts."

These were all his favorite dishes.

Cangshu Bai didn't speak; he only curled his fingers slightly, tightening his grip on the hand she held. The indifference that usually froze his eyes melted into a faint, gentle warmth, and even his breathing softened.

Someone passed by the door.

"Hey, have you read that new *History of the Green-Clad Beauty*?"

"No, I wanted to buy it, but the print shop that published it was blown up! Now, those first copies sold are worth a fortune!"

"I have one! I bought a copy the moment it hit the shelves. Tell you what, come to my place today, and I’ll lend it to you. You have no idea—the romance between the Red Ling Fairy and the Green-Clad Guest is truly scandalous—ouch!"

The man tripped, his foot catching on something, and he tumbled down the stairs. His friend rushed to help him up. The former kept yelping in pain, while the latter hurriedly took him to the clinic.

It seemed they wouldn't have time to appreciate *The History of the Green-Clad Beauty* for now.

Cangshu Bai lowered his eyes, lost in thought, when a cup of warm tea was pressed into his hand. It was very warm.

He looked up slightly and saw his wife’s smiling face.

"Have a sip of tea to warm up first. The food will be here soon."

Cangshu Bai’s lips moved slightly. "Okay."

The waiter noted the order, exited the room, and closed the door behind him.

Mu Ran poured herself a cup of tea. Just as she took a sip, Cangshu Bai suddenly leaned in close, his fingers supporting her chin, and he lowered his head to kiss her.

The moment their lips touched, the fragrance of the tea mixed with her faint, clean scent, winding and tangling between his lips and teeth.

He didn't kiss her deeply; he simply pressed against her, quietly sucking away the warmth and heat from her lips, which was even more tormenting than a deep kiss.

Mu Ran froze for a moment, her earlobes instantly turning hot. The teacup in her hand wobbled, and the tea nearly spilled, but his other hand steadied it firmly.

After a moment, he pulled back.

Mu Ran said nervously, "We’re in public, what are you doing?"

If someone had burst in, she wouldn't have the face to see anyone.

His thumb gently stroked her moist corner of her lips. "You said it yourself—have a sip of tea to warm up."

Mu Ran covered her burning face. "That’s not what I meant!"

He chuckled, his eyes shimmering.

The cold fish hidden in his sleeve secretly poked its head out, curiously watching its master’s current appearance.

It was like this every time.

Perhaps it was for revenge, perhaps for seizing rare treasures, or perhaps for survival—every time he returned from a slaughter, he would be exceptionally affectionate and lingering with his wife.

And then, his killing intent would be soothed, and he would no longer be that sinister, cold-blooded cultivator, but just an ordinary man.

Humans truly had two faces.

As Cangshu Bai lowered his eyes, the cold fish received a command and its body trembled.

No, please! It only liked eating treasures; it didn't want to be a little thief at night and eat the *History of the Green-Clad Beauty* hidden in people's homes!

If it ate those things, would it really not turn into a little yellow fish?

chapters.title: Slaughter
chapters.content:
The sky was growing dark as Old Man Longjian ran desperately through the bamboo forest.

He was covered in wounds and in a wretched state; the bloodstain on his neck was particularly shocking. Had it not been for his many years of cultivation, he would have long since perished under Hong Fu’s torture.

Old Man Longjian had thought he was going to die at Hong Fu’s hands, but unexpectedly, a masked person in black had appeared, wounded Hong Fu, and saved him. However, after rescuing him, the person in black had vanished without a trace.

Old Man Longjian had no time to ponder this; his only thought now was to escape.

That detestable devil behind him had snatched away all his treasures and left him severely wounded, reducing him to a prisoner under Hong Fu. Even more infuriating was that these cultivators still did not know the treasures were no longer in his possession, and they still treated him like a prized catch.

Old Man Longjian could only swallow this humiliation for now. Once he made a comeback, he would personally kill the person who had schemed against him from the shadows!

"It’s Old Man Longjian! Stop!"

Numerous figures suddenly appeared. The weapons in their hands glinted with cold light, and pairs of greedy eyes were fixed upon the old man.

In the blink of an eye, Old Man Longjian was completely surrounded.

One cultivator said, "Fellow Daoists, we all discovered Old Man Longjian together. Why don't we come to an agreement? Let us act on behalf of heaven and clear out this traitor for Red Flame Peak?"

Another replied, "What you say is true. Old Man Longjian is ungrateful and kills his fellow practitioners; his crimes are unforgivable. Perhaps the strange demons that have been appearing frequently are also his doing. It is our duty to slay demons and uphold justice."

A third person chimed in, "As for his treasures, if they fall into the hands of those with ill intentions, I fear it will stir up another bloody storm. I think we should divide them among ourselves for safekeeping to avoid further trouble. What do you all think?"

The others exchanged glances, their expressions shifting several times before they all nodded.

"That makes sense."

"That would be perfect."

"I have no objections."

...

These seemingly polished and respectable cultivators used such high-sounding excuses, appearing righteous while having already carved up Old Man Longjian in advance.

As for whether Old Man Longjian had any objections, that was unimportant.

Old Man Longjian had done plenty of wicked things himself, but now that he was reduced to meat on the chopping block, he desperately wanted to curse this group of beasts in human skin, yet he could not utter a single word due to the restrictions placed upon him.

The cultivators exchanged a look and rushed forward, unable to wait any longer.

Though they spoke of dividing the treasures, who among them didn't want to be the first to seize Old Man Longjian’s Qiankun bag?

Old Man Longjian knew he was in a dead end. He could only mobilize the little cultivation he had left to fight them to the death.

However, unexpectedly, the moment he mobilized his cultivation, it felt as if a fire were burning inside his body, and this heat spread throughout his entire frame at an alarming speed.

A cultivator realized something was wrong. "Not good, retreat!"

But it was too late.

A fire snake erupted from Old Man Longjian’s body, rapidly coiling around the surrounding cultivators. Wherever the crimson flame-tail swept, robes instantly charred and curled, flesh emitted a sizzling sound, and screams exploded one after another.

This fire snake was no ordinary flame; it was more like a fierce demonic fire. It grew more intense the more it coiled, actually burrowing into the cultivators' spiritual meridians. No matter how they tried to resist with their internal energy or slash with their swords, it only made the fire burn more fiercely.

Old Man Longjian finally realized what was happening. His eyes were bloodshot and filled with hatred, his soul screaming in madness—

Hong Fu!

Sure enough, the next moment, a crimson long whip swept through with a gust of wind. With a crisp "crack," the two closest cultivators didn't even have time to finish their screams before their bodies were shattered at the waist by the fire whip, their spraying blood and flesh instantly incinerated into ash by the flames.

A stunning red figure stepped slowly out of the firelight. Her face was as beautiful as a blooming peony, but her eyes were steeped in bone-chilling poison. It was none other than Hong Fu, who had been rumored to be severely wounded.

She flicked her wrist, and the fire whip coiled and slithered like a living snake. Wherever it passed, the cultivators' protective spiritual light shattered upon contact, and their meridians were scorched inch by inch by the strange fire.

All the magical treasures left behind after these corpses were burned fell into Hong Fu’s hands.

Old Man Longjian’s eyes were splitting with rage. The fire poison in his dantian was being stirred into a frenzy by her, and his meridians were in agonizing pain.

So, from the moment he was "saved," this had been a trap.

Hong Fu desperately needed rare treasures to break through a bottleneck that had remained unchanged for two hundred years, but Old Man Longjian had refused to reveal where he had hidden the treasures. It just so happened that these cultivators were eyeing her greedily from behind, so she gave them an opportunity.

She had long since tampered with Old Man Longjian’s body. The moment those cultivators approached, they would be entangled by her poisonous fire, and then she could simply walk out like this and harvest their heads one by one.

Old Man Longjian watched in shock as the surrounding cultivators died one by one in the scorching flames. He then saw Hong Fu’s whip coil around one of the cultivators, pulling him into her grasp. She pressed her hand onto the cultivator’s head, and to his horror, she was actually absorbing the man’s cultivation into her own body.

Old Man Longjian’s eyes widened in shock.

When did Hong Fu start walking the path of a demonic cultivator!

The line between the Dao and the demonic is but a single thought. Two hundred years ago, the proud and arrogant Hong Fu had developed a heart demon, and now, to break through her cultivation realm, she would stop at nothing.

The cultivators who had been clamoring to divide up Old Man Longjian just a moment ago were now nothing but corpses littering the ground.

"Since you refuse to reveal the location of the treasure, then take that secret to the grave with you!"

Hong Fu swept her whip, and Old Man Longjian’s body shattered, his soul torn to pieces. In his unwillingness, he turned to dust and vanished into the air without a trace.

Two maidservants appeared and stood respectfully behind Hong Fu.

Hong Fu’s murderous intent began to subside. "Spread the word: these people were hunting Old Man Longjian, and in his desperation, he detonated his dantian, perishing with them."

One maidservant nodded. "Yes."

The other maidservant said, "Immortal, there are many corpses on the other side of the bamboo forest. They are from Zhenyue Mountain City."

Hong Fu raised an eyebrow. "Let’s go take a look."

Cangshu Haoxue and his party had tried to pay their respects to Hong Fu several times before but had been rejected. After being turned away, Cangshu Haoxue had spoken no kind words, and the two maidservants had a deep impression of this group.

Even though they had been dead for several days, the frost covering them preserved the gruesome state of their deaths.

When Hong Fu arrived, the people from Zhenyue Mountain City happened to have arrived as well.

Among the dead was the Third Young Master of Zhenyue Mountain City, but the people who had come to collect the bodies showed little emotional change.

"I am Cangshu Fenming of Zhenyue Mountain City, greetings to Immortal Hong Fu." The young man was handsome and looked quite scholarly and refined. "I have come to collect the Third Young Master’s body. I wonder if the Immortal has any knowledge regarding the circumstances of his death?"

chapters.title: Warming Hands
chapters.content:
Hong Fu cast a cold glance at the corpse on the ground. "The Red Plum White Jade Umbrella."

Cangshu Fenming also said, "Indeed, we can see that the Third Young Master died under the Red Plum White Jade Umbrella, which is the magical artifact of the Elder of the Long Sword."

But did the hunted Elder of the Long Sword truly still have the strength to slaughter the people of the Cangshu family?

Hong Fu remained silent; naturally, she could not admit that she had already killed the Elder of the Long Sword.

Cangshu Fenming raised his hand and waved it. His subordinates lit a stick of incense on the ground.

Hong Fu asked, "What is this for?"

Cangshu Fenming replied, "Every time a member of the Cangshu family leaves home, they must leave behind a drop of blood. If they die, this drop of blood is used to create a Soul-Burning Incense.
