By utilizing this sliver of a lingering soul, we can reenact the scene before their death, making it easier for us to track down the culprit."

Of course, ordinary disciples did not receive the privilege of the Cangshu family seeking revenge for them; only those with the noble bloodline of the Cangshu family were entitled to this.

As the incense smoke swirled, a light drizzle appeared in the surroundings. In the blink of an eye, they were transported back to the day Cangshu Haoxue died.

However, since it was only a Soul-Burning Incense made from a single drop of blood, the projected images were somewhat intermittent.

"So what if the Eldest Young Master is called a rare genius of the century? None of us respect him."

"And the Second Young Master, his background... tsk, that goes without saying."

"The Fourth Young Master is still young; he’s just a fool."

"Only the Third Young Master is the one everyone looks forward to."

Cangshu Haoxue smiled and said, "Once I ascend to the position of family head, the first thing I will do is take down Red Flame Peak and make Hong Fu my bed-warming concubine."

The two handmaidens flared up on the spot.

"Arrogant!"

"Shameless!"

A hint of chill appeared in Hong Fu’s eyes.

The next moment, someone shouted, "It’s a trap!"

The Red Plum White Jade Umbrella suddenly appeared. The figure under the umbrella was blurry and indistinct, and that flash of green clothing looked even more ethereal in the bamboo forest’s drizzle.

Hong Fu’s expression changed.

The Soul-Burning Incense burned out, and everything returned to its original state.

Cangshu Fenming bowed to Hong Fu in apology. "The Third Young Master spoke foul words. Now that he is dead, let bygones be bygones. I hope Fairy Hong Fu will not take offense."

Hong Fu said coldly, "If he were still alive, even if the Zhenyue Mountain City were backing him, I would still tear out his tongue."

Cangshu Fenming did not dispute this. He said, "That was indeed the Red Plum White Jade Umbrella, but is the person wielding it necessarily the Elder of the Long Sword?"

Hong Fu was displeased. "Are you questioning me?"

Cangshu Fenming lowered his head again, saying respectfully, "After the Third Young Master spoke disrespectfully to you, he was brutally murdered. I merely thought that perhaps the person who struck could not bear to hear you being insulted, and thus could not help but act."

His words caused a slight stir in Hong Fu’s heart, but as she wore a veil, others could not see the change in her expression.

Cangshu Fenming observed Hong Fu secretly for a moment before saying, "I was just joking. You are as pure as ice and jade; if anyone dared to be disrespectful to you, I imagine others would find it unbearable. Furthermore, although the Elder of the Long Sword has defected from the sect, he did have a master-disciple relationship with you. Besides, the Third Young Master was hunting the Elder of the Long Sword, so it is only logical that he would strike back."

Hong Fu did not respond.

Cangshu Fenming bowed again. "We must return to report our findings. We shall take our leave now."

The members of the Cangshu family collected the corpse from the ground, and after a moment, they opened a scroll and vanished from the spot.

The two handmaidens looked at each other.

"Fairy, was it really the Elder of the Long Sword who killed them?"

"Regardless of who killed them, they deserved to die for being disrespectful to me."

The image of that green-clad figure still floated before Hong Fu’s eyes, as if spanning two hundred years of time, overlapping with the figure who had grabbed her in the secret realm and pushed her into the formation.

Beneath her veil, she bit her lip slightly. A sour and burning sensation clogged her chest, making her very soul tremble.

If not for him, her Dao heart would not have been affected, nor would she have developed a heart demon.

She cast aside the indescribable emotions in her heart and made a firm decision.

If they were to meet again one day, she would either kill him or die by his hand—there was no third path.

***

"Godfather, you are right. The Elder of the Long Sword escaping from Hong Fu was a setup from the start. Hong Fu used this opportunity to kill many cultivators, absorb their cultivation, and seize their magical treasures. I suspect that before long, Hong Fu will break through to the Nascent Soul stage."

"Although there are rumors spreading that those dead cultivators perished together with the Elder of the Long Sword, many of the dead were elite disciples of major sects. I fear those sects will not let Hong Fu off the hook in the shadows."

"That woman Hong Fu truly has methods and a ruthless heart. I don't think this is over yet. You were right to take Godmother and leave."

If Cangshu Bai had remained in that precarious town, the fire would have eventually reached him. If Cangshu Bai were still the same Cangshu Bai as before, he would not fear the wind and rain, thinking only that the rougher the waves, the more valuable the fish. But things were different now; he was a man with a family.

"Jinzhi, what are you thinking about?"

Cangshu Bai leaned against the carriage door, holding the reins. Hearing this, he opened his black eyes. The girl’s face was clearly reflected in his gaze, adding a bright and lighthearted color to his dark eyes.

"I was thinking that it will probably snow again soon, and the road might become difficult to travel."

Mu Ran smiled. "I bought a map. There should be a town ahead. If the road is bad, we can find a place to rest."

He nodded, then reached for the fur cloak draped over her shoulders, pulling the collar tight to keep the cold wind out. "Go back into the carriage and stay there. Don't come out and catch a chill."

Mu Ran replied, "You bought me such an expensive fur cloak, I'm not cold at all. I was bored inside, so I wanted to come out and keep you company and talk to you."

She took his hand. "Jinzhi, your hands are so cold."

For the past five days, Cangshu Bai had been driving the carriage, facing the biting wind. She was afraid he would freeze, but he kept saying it was fine and that in a few more days, they would reach his hometown.

Cangshu Bai lowered his eyes, his hand being warmed by hers. He said, "They aren't cold anymore."

Mu Ran tucked his hand under her fur cloak and used both of her hands to cover the one holding the reins, muttering, "Your hands are so beautiful; it would be a shame if you got frostbite."

He said in a low voice, "I won't."

"How can you be so sure?" Mu Ran argued logically. "Minor illnesses appear when you aren't paying attention. You're a doctor, how can you not understand this?"

He was very good-tempered. "I am foolish."

Mu Ran ducked into the carriage, and after a moment, she came back out holding something. "Use this to warm your hands. Don't be stingy with money; we have quite a bit of savings now."

He was handed a hand warmer. Unlike ordinary ones, this hand warmer was exquisitely carved, depicting little fish playing under lotus leaves in the water. It was a small wooden sphere that emitted warmth powered by spirit stones, a piece of masterful craftsmanship.

She was often reluctant to spend money on things that consumed spirit stones, yet she had taken this out to warm his hands.

Cangshu Bai asked, "Did you make this?"

Mu Ran nodded. "Yes, I made it."

He asked again, "Am I the only one who has one?"

Mu Ran laughed. "Yes, I only made this one. I didn't intend to have Boss Song sell it for me, so in this whole world, only Jinzhi has one."

Cangshu Bai’s fingertips touched the small object emitting warmth, feeling as if the carved lotus leaves were swaying and the fish had come to life.

He said, "Ranran, I like it very much."

chapters.title: I’ll Stay With You
chapters.content:
Cang Shubai’s hometown was a small place called Bishui Town, which was under the jurisdiction of Song City. It was considered a prosperous town, and because it was not far from Biyun Mountain, the public security there was quite good.

Cang Shubai’s parents had both passed away, and he had no other relatives. It was only after meeting Boss Hu, who appreciated his talent as a physician, that he left his homeland to make a living elsewhere with the owner of the medical clinic.

He never expected that while living as a stranger in a foreign land, he would meet Mu Ran. That was how he found a bond, a sense of longing, and a small home of his own.

Fortunately, the roads were not blocked by heavy snow during their journey. They traveled by carriage for nearly half a month and finally arrived safely in Bishui Town. The carriage stopped in front of a small, long-vacant house, drawing a few curious glances from passersby.

The young man, with his cold and aloof temperament, stepped out of the carriage first. He then reached out his hand to help the exquisitely beautiful woman descend slowly.

The two acted with intimacy and were a well-matched pair; one could tell at a glance that they were husband and wife.

Cang Shubai pushed open the gate, and a quiet, elegant courtyard with green tiles came into view. A few stalks of winter bamboo were planted in the yard, the stone table and stools were neat, and plain-colored gauze lanterns hung under the veranda—there was not a hint of ostentation.

Mu Ran walked into the courtyard first, looking around with curiosity. Her brows curved, and she said softly, "It’s so quiet and elegant here. So this is the kind of environment Jinzhi grew up in."

Cang Shubai watched her graceful figure as she moved to the stone table under the tree.

She lightly touched the stone table and looked back with a smile. "Did you sit here to read and eat snacks when you were a child?"

Cang Shubai’s lips curled slightly. "Yes. Sometimes I would practice writing here, too. But when I was young, my grip on the brush was always wrong, so I was often scolded by my father and punished with an hour or two of calligraphy practice. That was a common occurrence."

"No wonder your handwriting is so beautiful now." Mu Ran imagined what Cang Shubai looked like as a child, her eyes shining brightly. "Jinzhi is perfect at everything, but it must have been very cute to see you looking distressed over things you weren't good at when you were little."

Cang Shubai walked slowly toward her and gently wrapped his arms around her waist from behind. His grip was light, yet carried a hint of reluctance to let go. He rested his chin slightly on her shoulder, his warm breath falling softly against her neck.

The shoulder line that was usually tense in his daily life relaxed completely, and even the indifference in his eyes faded for the most part. He shed all his sharpness and defenses, like someone who had finally found a place to return to, leaning quietly against her—a rare moment of complete relaxation.

Mu Ran let him hold her. She looked back at him and tapped his brow with her finger. "When you were little, did this part of you often furrow like this?"

He replied, "If I was being disobedient and getting punished, then yes."

Mu Ran still found it hard to imagine him being disobedient; after all, his image in her heart was far too perfect.

Cang Shubai said, "I'm sorry."

Mu Ran took hold of the hands wrapped around her waist and relaxed her body as well. "Why are you suddenly apologizing to me?"

"This is not a good time of year, yet I made you travel a long distance with me, enduring the wind, snow, and bitter cold to come to a place that is entirely foreign to you." He said in a low voice, "I'm sorry, I’ve made you suffer."

Mu Ran replied, "I don't think this is suffering. You have relatives in your heart that you miss; that is a good thing. I imagine that when you were young, they must have treated you very well, loving and protecting you, holding you in the palm of their hands, which is why you remember them so fondly even now and cannot let go."

She chuckled. "Just the thought that someone once held you in their heart and cherished you makes me feel happy. I don't feel aggrieved in the slightest."

Cang Shubai buried his face deeper into the crook of her neck, his nose brushing against her delicate skin. His breathing grew slightly heavy, and his usually calm and waveless aura now carried a hint of imperceptible softness.

Mu Ran let him hold her quietly for a good while. After a long time, she asked curiously, "You haven't been back for two years, yet this courtyard isn't dirty at all. I don't see any weeds around, and there isn't much dust either."

Cang Shubai said, "Before I left, I bought a talisman for cleanliness and stuck it on the door."

Mu Ran said, "That’s wonderful. I was thinking that since we arrived home today, I might have to help you clean the house until midnight."

Cang Shubai liked the word "home" that she used. No matter where they were, as long as she was by his side and said the word "home," his heart felt exceptionally settled.

Mu Ran was suddenly swept up into his arms. She instinctively wrapped her arms around the young man’s neck and looked up at him.

Cang Shubai lowered his head and kissed the corner of her lips. "You’ve worked hard these past few days. The house is clean, so go and lie down to rest."

Mu Ran did not object. She leaned against his chest with peace of mind, looking curiously at everything in the courtyard as he walked.

Underfoot was a path paved with bluestone slabs, flanked by the sparse shadows of winter bamboo. Where the wind passed, the bamboo leaves rustled, and dappled sunlight filtered through the gaps in the leaves, falling upon them, gentle and mottled.

Passing through the moon gate, they reached the inner courtyard chambers. Two orchids were planted in front of the door, their faint, elegant fragrance drifting over.

Cang Shubai walked slowly and steadily up the steps. When he pushed the door open, a room full of cleanliness and freshness greeted them. The windows were bright and the tables clean, the bed was covered with plain soft bedding, and the desk was tidy. Even the air held a warm, faint scent of sunshine—quiet and comfortable.

He said, "This is my room. It remains exactly as it was when I left home."

Mu Ran was placed on the bed to sit.

He crouched in front of her, held her ankles, and considerately took off her shoes and socks. "If you don't like the arrangement of the room, just tell me, and I will rearrange it."

Mu Ran watched as he stood up again.

He leaned down, untied her fur coat, and took off the thick, emerald-green jacket she was wearing. "After you rest for a few days, we will go up the mountain to pay our respects to my parents."

Perhaps finding Mu Ran’s wide-eyed, obedient gaze truly adorable, he couldn't help himself and cupped her face, pressing several dense, lingering kisses upon her.

Cang Shubai took off her outer garments, tucked her into the warm quilt, and smoothed the corners for her. He sat by the bed, his fingers lightly touching her cheek, his gaze growing increasingly tender.

This house had once been filled with blood, and it was only later that he had restored it bit by bit. Even though the house had been restored to its former appearance, with his relatives gone, the feeling of a "home" had ultimately vanished.

Two years ago, he had been drifting through storms of blood and gore, never imagining that two years later, he would return with a wife.

Now, she was lying on the wooden bed he had slept on since he was a child. Everything in this cold, lonely room seemed to have gained warmth because of her.

Mu Ran grabbed his hand. "You’ve been traveling for so long, too. Won't you rest with me?"

He said, "I’ll go and unpack the luggage."

Mu Ran held onto his hand tightly. "I want to rest with you. The luggage can wait until later when we can do it together."

She threw out a reason he couldn't refuse: "Jinzhi, I can't sleep without you by my side."

Cang Shubai’s Adam's apple bobbed, his voice trembling slightly, "Alright, I’ll stay with you."

chapters.title: Unrefined
chapters.content:
In the past, when Cang Shubai practiced, he could remain in meditation for months at a time. A mere half-month journey was nothing to him in terms of fatigue.

But his wife needed him.

So, he lay down with her under the warm, comfortable quilt. After she closed her eyes and fell into a deep sleep, he opened his own, watching her beautiful sleeping face quietly. He listened to her steady, rhythmic breathing and pulled her gently into his arms, feeling a sense of peace he had never known before.

Mu Ran slept for over an hour. Once she was well-rested and her energy had returned, she pulled Cang Shubai up to help her unpack.

The carriage was almost entirely filled with their belongings, mostly due to Mu Ran; she felt everything was worth bringing along, and before they knew it, one wooden crate after another had piled up.

Unpacking took nearly another hour. Finally, Mu Ran stood before the wardrobe, taking the clothes out of the crates and hanging them up one by one.

Cang Shubai placed the glass lamp on the table and gave a slight wave of his hand. The lamp flickered to life, casting a gentle glow over the dim room. Looking back, he saw Mu Ran standing before the wardrobe, looking troubled.

He walked over and asked softly, "What’s wrong?"

Mu Ran touched her chin with one hand and said, "The wardrobe is a bit small; I’m running out of room to hang everything."

This was the room he used to live in, which was more than enough for one person's clothes, but now there were two. Furthermore, he was fond of buying her colorful, elaborate outfits, and they had brought two full crates of clothing this time. The wardrobe was indeed insufficient.

Cang Shubai reached out and pushed his own clothes into a single, folded pile, instantly freeing up a good amount of space in the wardrobe. "This should be better."

Mu Ran glanced at his clothes, now pitifully squeezed into a corner, taking up less than a third of the space. She fell silent for a moment. "Won't this make it seem like I'm treating you unfairly?"

He chuckled behind her. "I am more than happy to do so."

Mu Ran looked up at him.

In the warm candlelight, the young man’s features appeared exceptionally soft. A few stray locks of hair fell across his forehead, his nose was straight and refined, and his lips curved into a gentle arc. When he smiled, the corners of his eyes crinkled slightly, like a pool of warm spring water.

He was naturally handsome and elegant, yet he usually carried an air of cold detachment that made him seem unapproachable. Only at times like this, in front of her, would he retract his sharp edges, his temperament becoming as warm and polished as jade, making him all the more captivating.

Mu Ran’s eyes sparkled as if they were studded with stars.

Cang Shubai lowered his gaze, his fingers gently brushing the corner of her eye. He whispered, "Why are you looking at me like that?"

They had been married for two years, and she had looked at him this way countless times. He knew exactly why she looked at him like that, but he wanted to hear her say it.

Sure enough, Mu Ran turned around and hugged him. "Jinzhi, I think you’ve become even better-looking."

When Cang Shubai was a child, he had heard neighbors say he was a handsome boy. Later, after his family was destroyed and he embarked on the path of cultivation for the sake of revenge, he had teachers, but most of them only sought to manipulate and use him.

On that bloody path, he sometimes had to live like a vermin in the shadows just to survive. As for his appearance, he had never cared.

But over these past two years, having been told he was handsome so many times, he had vaguely begun to realize that his looks were perhaps not bad.

He didn't need to be perfect; he only needed to captivate her alone.

Cang Shubai rested his chin on the top of her head, his large hand gently stroking her back, the corners of his lips curling upward.

But before he could enjoy the intimacy for long, Mu Ran pulled away from his embrace. "If you fold your clothes like that, they’ll get wrinkled. Aren't there other rooms? Let’s put the clothes that don't fit in the wardrobe in the next room."

Cang Shubai adjusted to the sudden emptiness in his arms for a moment before nodding. "Alright."

He picked up the crate and walked toward the next room.

Mu Ran followed behind him, unable to resist looking outside once more.

Beyond the courtyard wall was another house.

A figure stood on the second floor, seemingly watching them work with curiosity.

Mu Ran didn't like the feeling of being watched, but she told herself she might be overthinking it; perhaps the person over there was just standing there to catch the breeze.

Cang Shubai looked back. "Ranran."

Mu Ran snapped out of her thoughts and hurried over to push the door open.

As Cang Shubai walked into the room, he cast a subtle glance behind him.

The figure opposite them quickly shrank back and vanished without a trace.

The sky grew dark as night fell.

Cang Shubai watched Mu Ran organizing the clothes and said, "I’m going to the street to buy some food. What would you like to eat?"

They hadn't prepared any ingredients today, and they were tired, so they naturally didn't intend to cook dinner themselves.

Mu Ran thought for a moment and said, "I’d like some wonton noodles."

Cang Shubai patted her head. "Wait for me to return."

Not long after he stepped out of the house, a figure followed behind him.

"Young master, young master, please wait!"

The person who caught up was a middle-aged man with a handlebar mustache, the same one who lived in the house opposite. He wore an enthusiastic and friendly expression.

Cang Shubai walked through the alley without stopping.

The man followed persistently. "I live across from you, so we are neighbors now. It is fate that we have met. I would like to make friends with you. I see that you have an extraordinary air about you; I wonder if you are interested in the path of immortality?"

Cang Shubai stopped and looked at him calmly.

The man said, "How old do you think I am?"

Cang Shubai remained silent.

The man laughed heartily. "You probably think I’m only in my forties, but I am actually over a hundred years old! This is because I joined the Changqing Sect. Through dedicated practice, immortality is not out of reach. I see that you and your wife are deeply in love, and your wife is a rare beauty, but mortals only have a lifespan of a hundred years. In less than twenty years, that beautiful woman will be a withered old crone. Don't you find that a pity?"

Cang Shubai said, "It is indeed a pity."

The man’s eyes lit up, and he quickly produced an invitation. "The Changqing Sect is not a place just anyone can enter. Since I have an affinity with you, I am willing to vouch for you and recommend you for the Changqing Sect. How about it?"

Cang Shubai took the invitation and asked, "You wish to recommend me to the Changqing Sect—has anyone else been told of this?"

The Cold Fish quietly poked its head out.

The man shook his head and said, "I only noticed today that you and your beautiful wife had moved into the house opposite mine. At first glance, I realized I had a deep connection with you, so I haven't had time to tell my fellow disciples. I couldn't wait to invite you to join."

Unable to suppress his excitement and impatience, the man added, "If you go and inquire, you will know how hard it is to get into the Changqing Sect. As long as you sign this invitation, you can go to the sect to attend lectures. Oh, and your wife, too! Bring your wife along. Once you enter the Changqing Sect, I guarantee you won't—"

A flash of cold light, and the man’s head fell to the ground, his mouth still opening and closing. "—regret it..."

A moment later, he saw his own headless corpse collapse. He seemed to realize what had happened; his expression was one of shock, but the light in his eyes faded rapidly. His pale face froze in a stiff expression as he breathed his last.

The Cold Fish darted out from its master’s sleeve and swallowed the soul before it could dissipate.

It knew that whenever its master asked a poor wretch if anyone else knew about the situation, it was only to make killing them easier.

"A 'Life-Borrowing Invitation'—a crude, unrefined trick."

The invitation turned to ash in the young man's hand and vanished.

At the same time, the severed corpse on the ground was covered in frost and snow.

As he turned to leave, his long sleeves fluttered, and the corpse on the ground dissolved into icy mist and dissipated.

chapters.title: Sickeningly Sweet
chapters.content:
Mu Ran had settled down for the time being in Bishui Town with Cang Shubai. The long journey had truly been exhausting, and for several days in a row, she had lazed in bed until the sun was high in the sky.

Cang Shubai indulged her laziness; he was the one who went out to buy groceries, cooked the meals, and washed the clothes. In short, by the time the sluggish Mu Ran crawled out of bed, he had already finished all the household chores.

Today was no exception.

The sun rose, slightly dispelling the winter chill. The frost that had formed on the ground in the morning slowly turned into water vapor and vanished, though the air still nipped at one’s nose with every breath.

Although it was still early, Cang Shubai was already busy in the kitchen preparing the midday meal.

Mu Ran liked chicken and mushroom soup. If it was stewed for an hour or two in advance, the meat would become even more tender and succulent—the texture she loved best.

The young man, dressed in a blue and white robe, had his sleeves neatly rolled up to his forearms, revealing a pair of slender yet strong wrists. His movements were steady and light as he sliced the vegetables; as the blade rose and fell, the mushrooms and chicken were arranged with perfect precision, not a hint of disorder to be seen.

The warm glow of the stove fire reflected off his profile. His long lashes drooped, casting soft shadows, and his usually cold, aloof features were now filled with nothing but focus.

The cold fish swam freely in the water jar. Every time this happened, it couldn't help but poke its head out to take a look.

Its master possessed profound cultivation and had long since reached the stage of *bigu*—he didn't need to eat at all. Yet, he insisted on finding trouble for himself, making things so complicated; he had to cook the meals and light the fires himself.

It was as if he had practiced his cultivation for nothing.

He had never seen anyone so foolish.

A slender figure quietly approached the doorway again.

The cold fish skillfully and hurriedly lowered its head, hiding beneath the water's surface, pretending it didn't exist.

Cang Shubai had long since heard the deliberately softened footsteps and felt the gaze fixed intently upon him. However, he acted as if he didn't care, not even turning his head to look, simply lowering his eyes to focus on his work.

Mu Ran poked her head out from outside the door, peeking stealthily for a long time.

She didn't know what was wrong with her; it seemed to be for no reason at all, but she just felt that Cang Shubai looked exceptionally handsome whenever he was focused.

The way his eyes drooped was handsome, the curve of his falling hair was handsome, and those bony, delicate hands with their distinct knuckles were also handsome.

This man, perfect in every way, was her husband.

Joy filled Mu Ran’s heart. She lifted her skirt, tried to move as quietly as possible, and crept closer.

The cold fish in the water glanced at its seemingly indifferent master, whose lips were actually slightly curled upward. No matter how cold he appeared on the outside, he was likely already feeling quite pleased on the inside.

*Tsk, humans. This routine again.*

Finally, Mu Ran hugged the man’s waist from behind, leaning dependently against his back. Breathing in his scent, she purred comfortably, "Jinzhi."

She didn't know why she called his name; she didn't need a purpose, she just wanted to say it.

Cang Shubai placed the ingredients into the clay pot without haste, covered it, and let it simmer over a low flame. Afterward, he rinsed his hands in a basin, and Mu Ran thoughtfully offered him a dry towel to wipe them.

Once his hands were clean and dry, he turned to face her. With one arm around her body and the other brushing her hair, he said softly, "Did you sleep well?"

Mu Ran nodded. "I slept well."

"Go wash up. I made porridge; have a little to tide you over."

She nodded obediently but remained lingering in his arms, refusing to move.

Cang Shubai leaned down and pressed a kiss to the top of her head. "Ranran, be good."

At this, Mu Ran seemed to draw enough strength. Full of energy, she lifted her face, kissed his jaw, left his embrace, and went off to wash up, happy as could be.

In the water jar, the little blue fish blew a few more bubbles.

*Tsk, humans. It’s sickeningly sweet.*

After lunch that day, Cang Shubai took Mu Ran up the mountain to pay respects to his parents.

In the winter, the mountains were even colder. Even hunters wouldn't stay in the mountains to hunt at this time of year. They didn't see anyone else on the path, but fortunately, there was no ice on the trail, otherwise, it would have been truly impossible to climb.

Cang Shubai said, "I'll carry you."

Mu Ran was breathing slightly heavily, hot air puffing from her mouth. She shook her head and said, "I can walk myself. There's no need to carry me."

He knew she was afraid of tiring him out.

Whenever this happened, a strong impulse would rise within Cang Shubai. He wanted to tell her his true identity and reveal his power before her—shrinking the earth to inches, flying on a sword; none of it would be a challenge.

But she was just an ordinary girl.

If she knew he was steeped in deep karmic sin, would she be afraid or uneasy?

If she knew that when he first married her, his only goal was to spend a hundred years as husband and wife before parting ways in life and death, never to cross paths again, would she loathe him?

She often spoke to him of what she had heard: that cultivators often schemed against one another, and sects frequently slaughtered each other. She didn't want to have too much to do with those so-called cultivators. If she found out his identity and asked for a divorce, what then?

How ridiculous. He had always been decisive in killing and had used many despicable means, yet when it came to Mu Ran, he was cowardly and timid, lacking even the courage to take a gamble.

Mu Ran sensed that something was wrong with Cang Shubai’s mood. She looked up and asked, "Jinzhi, what’s wrong?"

He bent down, bringing his face closer to hers, dark light flickering in his obsidian eyes. "Ranran."

Mu Ran: "Hmm?"

Vaguely, faint purple specks seemed to shimmer in his eyes. Mu Ran was staring at him with her whole heart and naturally had no defenses. Her gaze slowly turned vacant, she lost consciousness, and she fell forward into the young man’s arms.

Cang Shubai picked her up, kissed her forehead, and with a light tap of his toes, he rose from the ground like a startled swan.

The grip in his arms was steady and gentle, shielding her securely against his chest and blocking the biting cold wind. As his robes fluttered, he swept over layers of emerald treetops.

In just a moment, they landed steadily on the mountaintop.

He set her down gently, his fingertips still lingering affectionately on her waist. Lifting her face again, he kissed the corner of her lips, a dark light flickering in his eyes, and whispered, "Ranran, we’re here."

Mu Ran’s eyes suddenly regained their luster, as if waking from a dream. She looked up to see the sea of clouds and the vast sky. She was slightly dazed, touched her head, and felt a bit confused.

Cang Shubai lightly flicked the tip of her nose. "I told you last night not to hide under the covers and sneakily read storybooks. You must have slept until you were muddled, and with the long walk up the mountain, is your head feeling a bit dizzy?"

Mu Ran nodded. "A little."

He said, "No staying up late to read storybooks today."

She felt a bit guilty. "Alright, I understand."

chapters.title: Stars
chapters.content:
Two evergreen trees were planted in front of the graves of Cang Shubai’s parents. They were lush and leafy, remaining green throughout the year like two silent figures standing guard over a patch of pure earth, where not even a single weed could be found.

He turned back, gently took Mu Ran’s hand, and spoke in a low, soft, yet solemn voice: "Father, Mother, this is Ranran, my wife."

Mu Ran knelt down beside him and said respectfully, "Father, Mother."

Cang Shubai did not tell her that this was a cenotaph, fearing she would overthink it. His parents’ remains had been lost two hundred years ago. Back then, he had been fledging, lacking both the ability to protect himself and the power to seek revenge. Even this cenotaph had only been erected by him in recent years.

He had already slaughtered the Cangshu family in Song City to the last person, yet now, kneeling before his parents’ graves, he felt no joy at all.

"Although I never met you, I know you must have been good people." Mu Ran kept her head down as she arranged the offerings, her murmurs never ceasing. "Thank you for bringing Jinzhi into this world, and thank you for raising him so well. Please rest assured, I will accompany Jinzhi well from now on and take good care of him until he’s plump and healthy."

"But if your spirits are in heaven and you are truly worried, you can send us a dream. Jinzhi often misses you; he wants to talk to you, too."

"But you don't need to worry too much. I know that while Jinzhi looks cold, he has the softest heart. He walked a very, very long road alone in the past, but with me here from now on, I won't let him be lonely again."

...

Cang Shubai knelt to the side, his blue robes fluttering softly in the mountain breeze. Perhaps it was the warmth of the sunlight, but his usually cold and indifferent eyes were now completely immersed in a gentle, tender glow.

He watched Mu Ran quietly, watching her bow her head to arrange the offerings with focus, watching her little mouth open and close as she chattered away to the two graves. Every word she spoke landed softly on the most tender part of his heart.

Finally, Mu Ran took his hand. "Father, Mother, Jinzhi and I will both be just fine, right?"

She looked up at him, her smile bright and radiant.

Cang Shubai felt a slight tightness in his throat. His fingertips curled involuntarily as he wrapped her hand in his large palm. His voice was slightly hoarse. "Right."

The sun had been high in the sky when they climbed the mountain, and it was already evening by the time they descended.

Back on the streets, the night was falling. Smoke curled from the chimneys of every household, and pedestrians hurried along, rushing home.

On the way back, Mu Ran no longer tried to be brave. She leaned on Cang Shubai’s back, squinting her eyes to sleep for a while. When she opened them again, they had already entered a quiet, deserted alley.

Mu Ran had noticed long ago that the alley where Cang Shubai’s ancestral home was located was sparsely populated and exceptionally quiet. On their first day, she had seen someone seemingly living across the street, but she hadn't seen a trace of them since. Perhaps she had just been mistaken.

Still feeling drowsy, Mu Ran lifted her eyes and said, "The stars are out."

Cang Shubai walked with a steady, even pace. Hearing this, he tilted his head slightly, a faint smile blooming at the corners of his lips. The person on his back was soft and warm, her breath brushing against his neck with a lingering trace of sleepiness.

He said, "Mm, I see them."

Mu Ran looked at the brightest star in the sky and reached out toward the night sky as if playing. "It’s so beautiful. It would be wonderful if I could pick it and keep it."

Cang Shubai said, "I will pick it for you."

Mu Ran was amused by him, knowing he was joking. She lowered her hand, wrapped her arms around his neck, and rubbed her face against his, saying lightheartedly, "No, I already have two of the most beautiful stars."

Her fingers lightly touched the corner of his left eye. "One star is hidden here."

Then, her fingers lightly touched the corner of his right eye. "And another star is hidden here."

She laughed joyfully, "Jinzhi, I’ve already picked the stars."

Cang Shubai’s eyelashes trembled slightly. When he looked up again, his pitch-black eyes were filled with shimmering light—truly brighter, gentler, and more scorching than the stars in the sky.

Mu Ran seemed infected by the brilliant stars, and her own clear, autumn-water eyes began to sparkle with points of light.

Cang Shubai asked in a low voice, "Want to kiss me?"

Mu Ran nodded.

He said, "I'll let you kiss me when we get home."

Her eyes curved into crescents, her smile captivating. "Okay."

When they reached their doorstep, they saw two men standing at the entrance across the street. Mu Ran, still feeling shy, quickly patted Cang Shubai’s shoulder and climbed off his back.

The two men wore identical dark-colored robes, appearing to be from the same sect. They exchanged a glance, walked over, bowed with cupped hands, and asked, "Are you two the residents of this house?"

Cang Shubai stepped aside to shield Mu Ran and said, "Yes."

One of the men asked, "Have you two seen our fellow disciple? His name is Duan Minggui, and he lives right across from you."

Cang Shubai’s tone was devoid of emotion. "We only moved here recently. We haven't met the person across the street, nor did we know anyone lived there."

The two men exchanged another look, then suddenly smiled in a friendly manner. "If you happen to see Duan Minggui later, please let us know. We are disciples of the Changqing Sect; our sect is located on Changqing Lane in Song City. It is fate that we met you here."

The other man took out two invitations. "If you and your wife are interested in pursuing the Great Dao of Longevity, feel free to leave your names on these invitations and bring them to our Changqing Sect to attend lectures and study the Dao."

Mu Ran looked at the two invitations with curiosity.

Cang Shubai said, "My wife and I have studied under a master before, but because our talent was lacking and we had no aptitude for cultivation, we left. We have no destiny for the Great Dao of Longevity. We appreciate your kindness, but we must decline."

He took Mu Ran’s hand and walked into their home. Once the door was shut, the friendliness vanished from the two men’s expressions.

"Our Changqing Sect is the most popular new sect in Song City right now. Who wouldn't want to join us? This man, however, actually looks down on it."

"They truly have no aptitude for cultivation. They were likely expelled from their previous sect and are disheartened."

"I could see their aptitude was poor, but the man is handsome and the woman is beautiful. Just for their looks—such fine physical vessels—many people would surely fight to have them."

"Enough. Recruiting them isn't urgent. Duan Minggui owes our sect so much lifespan yet has gone missing. I don't know if he ran away, but we had better find his whereabouts first."

The other man nodded. "That is true."

The two men walked away together, and the alley fell silent once more.

Cang Shubai boiled water and bathed with Mu Ran. Of course, it was just a simple bath; pitying her for the exhaustion of climbing the mountain today, he could not bear to do anything else to her.

When Mu Ran was picked up and tucked into the bedcovers to sleep, she grabbed his hand. "How about... I help you?"

Cang Shubai sat on the edge of the bed and touched her face. "Aren't you afraid your mouth will be sore?"

Mu Ran grabbed the quilt and covered her face.

He laughed out loud and patted her body gently. "Sleep."

He still had to clean up the dirty clothes and wash the mud-stained shoes.

Mu Ran slept very soundly. In the middle of the night, she had a dream. It felt as if something was spying on her; this damp, sinister gaze enveloped her from all directions, as if it had turned into a cold, venomous snake, tightly constricting her body.

Even her breathing seemed to become stifled. Finally, struggling against this feeling of confinement, she broke free from the dream and opened her eyes to see her husband’s eyes, deep as a cold pool.

There were no lights on in the room.

Cang Shubai sat on the edge of the bed. She didn't know how long he had been sitting there, just watching her quietly. A young man with such a cold and distant temperament now looked like a ghost.

Mu Ran was puzzled. "Jinzhi, aren't you sleeping?"

His eyes filled with a shimmering, gentle light again. He reached out and opened his palm, where points of light emerged. He whispered, "Look, what is this?"

Mu Ran perked up and crawled out of bed. As the quilt slid down, revealing her slender frame, the man had already thoughtfully pulled the quilt back up, wrapping her tightly.

She said, "It’s a glowing stone!"

Lying in his palm was a mineral emitting light. The glow was not harsh; it simply radiated a soft, gentle shimmer, as if he had condensed crushed starlight in his palm.

He asked, "Does it look like the star you saw tonight?"

Mu Ran nodded. "It does!"

She took the stone, and the dim room seemed to sparkle because of it. At this moment, she also noticed that Cang Shubai’s hair and shoulders were covered in a layer of frost, as if he had been to a place of extreme cold and was covered in wind and snow.

Mu Ran covered his hands. "Where did you go, and where did this stone come from?"

Cang Shubai said, "While I was washing the clothes, I saw a shooting star fall, so I chased after it and found this small fragment."

Mu Ran was astonished, unable to speak for a moment.

This world was bizarre and filled with monsters and ghosts, so a falling star didn't seem strange. What was strange was that someone would actually chase after a fallen star.

Cang Shubai leaned in closer, a faint smile rippling in his eyes, gentler than jade. "Ranran, do you like it?"

Mu Ran’s heart felt as if it had been poked in its softest spot. She reached out and hugged his cold body. "I like it."

He lowered his gaze. "As long as you like it."

"Jinzhi is a fool."

Cang Shubai’s voice was filled with laughter. "How am I a fool?"

"You ran out in the middle of the night. What if you had run into a demonic cultivator?" She used both hands to hug him even tighter. "Don't do this again."

His chin rested on the top of her head, his Adam's apple bobbed, and laughter spilled from his lips. "Mm, I won't do it again."

chapters.title: Satisfaction
chapters.content:
Cangshu Haoxue’s corpse was carried back to Zhenyue Mountain City. The elders and disciples guarding the mountain gate wore solemn expressions, though there was no sign of grief.

Cultivation is like this—a world of the strong preying on the weak, where no one can be certain they will live to see the next day’s sun.

However, Cangshu Haoxue was the Third Young Master of the Cangshu family. Even if he was not particularly capable, he represented Zhenyue Mountain City when outside. For someone to kill him was equivalent to slapping the face of Zhenyue Mountain City.

As the family head, Cangshu Taotian felt no sorrow looking at the mangled corpse of his son on the ground. He merely frowned, feeling displeasure and anger.

"Was it the old man Changjian who did this?"

Cangshu Fenming replied, "According to the Soul-Burning Incense, the Third Young Master was indeed killed by a man holding a red plum and white jade umbrella."

Cangshu Taotian, who was several hundred years old yet appeared quite young with his sword-like brows, starry eyes, and upright stature, possessed an inherent air of authority. "Where is the old man Changjian?"

"Shortly after the Third Young Master died, the old man Changjian perished along with the cultivators pursuing him. There is nothing left of his remains."

Cangshu Taotian snorted. "So, there is no proof left. Haoxue had many life-saving treasures on him; why did he die so easily?"

"According to the scene, the Third Young Master walked into a pre-arranged killing formation. The person who acted was highly skilled, and the Third Young Master was killed before he could react."

Cangshu Taotian said, "The old man Changjian was indeed skilled in formations. These methods align with his style."

Cangshu Fenming stood to the side without comment. He was only responsible for reporting the findings; the conclusions were none of his concern.

He continued, "While out on this mission, I discovered that the Cangshu branch family in Song City had been wiped out."

Cangshu Taotian’s gaze shifted. "Who did it?"

Cangshu Fenming said, "The branch family was wiped out cleanly, reduced to ashes by a fire. It is impossible to tell whose methods were used, and the precious Hongmeng Glazed Lamp in the possession of the branch family head has also gone missing."

The others began to murmur.

"Even if it is a branch family, they still carry the name of the Cangshu family."

"This is clearly not taking our Zhenyue Mountain City seriously!"

"Is someone deliberately targeting us, or is this just ordinary江湖 (jianghu) feuding?"

"Could it also be the work of the old man Changjian?"

"That’s right. The old man Changjian was severely injured two hundred years ago and never recovered. The Hongmeng Glazed Lamp is a supreme treasure for repairing the soul. It is not impossible that he wanted it to heal his wounds."

For a moment, the crowd was filled with righteous indignation.

Someone said, "Family Head, the Third Young Master was killed by the old man Changjian. Although the old man is dead, our reputation has been damaged. Are we just going to let it go?"

Cangshu Taotian’s eyes turned cold. "Naturally, we cannot let it go. Even if the old man is dead, his sect, Chiyan Peak, still exists. Since he used the methods of Chiyan Peak to kill, then Chiyan Peak must be held responsible."

The others vaguely understood what Cangshu Taotian meant.

Recently, the younger generation of the clan had been declining. Aside from the First Young Master, who had reached the Nascent Soul stage at a young age, there were no other exceptionally talented youths.

They needed more resources to cultivate more young people; even if they lacked talent, they had to be forced into having it.

It could be said that Cangshu Haoxue’s death provided them with a perfect excuse.

"Since we are going to war, I’ll take the vanguard."

Leaning against a tree was a young man, his red robes loosely tied, the hem fluttering in the wind.

Most striking was his crimson hair, neither tied nor crowned, falling casually over his shoulders and back. A few stray locks hung over his forehead, making his features appear all the more vivid and fierce.

When the others looked over, his eyes tilted slightly upward with a hint of careless, wicked charm, and his lips curled into a half-smile. Despite speaking of war and taking the vanguard, his demeanor was lazy and relaxed, without a hint of gravity.

Cangshu Taotian frowned slightly. "You are volunteering?"

Cangshu Qihua nodded with a smile. "Why not?"

He was Cangshu Taotian’s second son. His exotic appearance and crimson hair were symbols of his mother’s status as the lowliest medicine-tester in Zhenyue Mountain City.

Cangshu Qihua said, "However, if I am the one to take down Chiyan Peak, the heavenly treasures harvested there must be left for me to distribute. How about that?"

Cangshu Taotian pondered for a moment and said, "Agreed."

He turned and left, and the others followed. The remains on the ground were carried away by disciples for burial. Since Cangshu Haoxue had died so disgracefully, Zhenyue Mountain City would certainly not hold a funeral for him.

Cangshu Fenming looked at the frivolous red figure under the tree. "Is the Second Young Master leaving the mountain now?"

Cangshu Qihua laughed with an ambiguous tone. "If I don't leave now, and the other brothers get there first, wouldn't I end up with nothing?"

Cangshu Fenming dutifully reminded him, "Miss Mu will be coming to Zhenyue Mountain City in a few days."

"Is that so? Then please tell my fiancée that I have important business to attend to and no time to accompany her." Cangshu Qihua turned his back and waved lazily. "If she’s unhappy, just let her break off the engagement."

Cangshu Fenming watched Cangshu Qihua’s departing back and sighed slightly.

Of all the young masters of the Cangshu family, not a single one was easy to deal with.

In Song City, ever since the Cangshu family was wiped out, the newly established Changqing Sect had leaped to become the largest and most popular cultivation sect in the city.

Mu Ran was following Cangshu Bai to buy New Year’s goods. Walking down the street, she could hear people mentioning the name "Changqing Sect" from time to time.

Regardless of the sect, recruiting disciples usually required checking for cultivation talent, but the Changqing Sect was different. They claimed that even those without talent could be trained to have it, which made many ordinary people yearn for them.

Cangshu Bai reached out again, shielding Mu Ran behind him. "We are not interested in cultivation."

The black-robed disciple who had come to invite them looked disappointed but did not pester them further, only saying, "If you change your mind, just come to our Changqing Sect."

Mu Ran watched the man leave and said, "This is the first time I’ve seen a sect recruit like this. They really aren't picky at all."

She grabbed Cangshu Bai’s hand again and whispered, "When things are abnormal, there must be demons. Jinzhi, I think it’s better if we don’t get involved with the Changqing Sect. I don’t know why, but I find them a bit terrifying. Don’t you?"

Cangshu Bai nodded. "Yes, I find them terrifying too."

Mu Ran looked at him skeptically; her husband’s expression was calm, and she couldn't see any sign of fear.

He gently stroked her bangs with his fingertips. "But the matter of longevity is what many people desire in their hearts. Are you not tempted?"

Mu Ran’s eyes curved into a smile, full of warmth. "Didn't we agree when we got married? To be together for a hundred years, our hearts forever united. As long as I can spend this life with you, that is enough. As for longevity, one cannot force it, nor should one covet it. Being able to grow old with you is all the satisfaction I need."

Cangshu Bai knew that she had always been easily satisfied. In the past, if he peeled a few water chestnuts for her, she would hold them and be happy for a long time.

But he was not a man who was easily satisfied.

chapters.title: Double Standards
chapters.content:
A century is a lifetime for an ordinary person, but for a cultivator, a hundred years is far too short; a single period of seclusion can witness the changing of the world.

What he wanted was a thousand years, ten thousand years, life after life.

Cang Shubai fed her another candy pill, his fingertips lightly brushing her slightly puffed-out cheek. Meeting her clear, innocent eyes, he couldn't help but let a smile reach his own.

"Shall we go to the bookstore and see if there are any new storybooks?"

Mu Ran’s eyes lit up. "Let's go."

He took her hand and walked toward the bookstore across the street.

The shop was crowded. One customer was complaining to the owner, "Why is *The Amorous History of the Green-Clad* sold out?"

The owner said with a troubled expression, "Ever since the bookstore in Wufang City was blown up, *The Amorous History of the Green-Clad* has been out of print."

The customer, clearly wealthy, insisted, "You have wide connections, owner. If anyone who bought a copy before is willing to sell, I’ll pay a high price to buy it back!"

The owner quickly lowered his voice. "You’d better not talk like that now. Everyone who kept a copy of *The Amorous History of the Green-Clad* at home has seen ghosts at night!"

"Seen ghosts?"

The owner whispered, "They say that those who kept the book at home saw a blue ghost shadow in the middle of the night. The shadow is truly terrifying; wherever it passes, it leaves a chill and water stains. It must be a drowned ghost, and this drowned ghost is specifically here to eat books!"

The customer was skeptical. "Is there any logical connection between a drowned ghost and eating books?"

"Who can explain the affairs of demons and ghosts? In any case, everyone says the book *The Amorous History of the Green-Clad* is cursed. No bookstore dares to sell it. Better not mention it, better not mention it."

Mu Ran was standing on tiptoe, looking at the books on the shelf. When she looked up, she saw the young man’s lips slightly curled upward. Curious, she asked, "Is there something that makes you happy?"

Cang Shubai reached out and effortlessly took down the book she had been eyeing but couldn't reach due to her height. He placed it in her hands and whispered, "Being able to see you smile at me the moment I look down—does that count as something happy?"

Mu Ran was amused and let out a laugh. "Of course it does."

Cang Shubai patted her head. "Do you like this book?"

Mu Ran opened the book, titled *The Overbearing Demon Cultivator Falls for Me*. The first page read:

"No more... I can't take it anymore."

"Be good, you still have strength. Look, you’re holding me so tightly."

Mu Ran quickly closed the book, her face flushing slightly. She glanced up cautiously and caught his calm, unruffled gaze.

He couldn't have seen it, right?

A faint curve appeared on Cang Shubai’s lips.

Mu Ran lowered her head. She knew it; he definitely saw it.

But then she thought about it—sometimes in bed, before they went to sleep, he would flip through books with her and offer a critique or two. Suddenly, she didn't feel so shy anymore.

It was just that, usually, while critiquing, he would take off her clothes and force her to read the book aloud. At first, she would read smoothly, but later, every word she uttered would be fragmented. By the end, she would have no strength left to identify the characters on the page before being pulled into his arms.

Then, he would be the one reading, and every word he breathed into her ear would be exceptionally hot.

Mu Ran’s assessment of this was that he really knew how to play.

She stole another glance at him. Cang Shubai still wore that cold, indifferent expression.

She had heard Auntie Wang say many times that Cang Shubai was cold and aloof. Was he really easy to get along with?

Of course he was easy to get along with.

Whenever Mu Ran thought about the many sides of Cang Shubai that no one else saw, her heart filled with joy.

She hooked her little finger around his and gave it a gentle tug.

Cang Shubai quietly leaned down, his dark eyes filled entirely with her presence.

Mu Ran muttered, "Can I buy this book?"

He also whispered, "You can."

She looked at the people in the bookstore—people coming and going, and anyone could clearly see what book was in her hand. "I’m too embarrassed to go pay."

Cang Shubai skillfully took the book from her. "I’ll go."

Mu Ran smiled happily. "Jinzhi, you’re so good."

Cang Shubai had forgotten when he first started buying such books for Mu Ran, but he felt that for the sake of her saying "You’re so good," he would be willing to climb a mountain of blades or descend into a sea of fire.

However, Mu Ran would never bear to let him climb a mountain of blades or descend into a sea of fire; at most, she only asked him to buy some "spicy" books on her behalf. Thus, he had done it so often that it had become second nature.

Cang Shubai looked refined and scholarly, like a man of letters. Seeing him buying not the Four Books or Five Classics, but rather an improper storybook—and one that women liked to read at that—the owner couldn't help but take a few extra looks at him while ringing him up.

Mu Ran hid by the door, feeling apologetic.

But Cang Shubai, facing the judgmental gaze of others who saw him as a dissolute scholar, remained calm and composed. He paid, took the book, and walked out, only for Mu Ran to quickly snatch it and toss it into the *Qiankun* bag she had spent a fortune on.

Other cultivators used their *Qiankun* bags for magical treasures, but hers was packed full of New Year’s supplies.

Cang Shubai said, "You didn't eat much at noon. Let's go buy something to eat."

Mu Ran nodded and pulled him toward a stall selling crispy pastries.

"Godfather, this is terrible! People from the Zhenyue Mountain City have actually gone to the Chiyan Peak to cause trouble!"

Dr. Hu’s voice echoed in Cang Shubai’s mind. Cang Shubai remained unmoved, focusing only on the back of Mu Ran as she haggled with the stall owner.

Dr. Hu was used to being ignored. He continued to transmit his voice, "They say the Third Young Master of Zhenyue Mountain City, Cangshu Haoxue, died at the hands of Old Man Longjian. Also, a branch family of the Cangshu clan was wiped out, supposedly by Old Man Longjian as well. So, Zhenyue Mountain City is demanding an explanation from Chiyan Peak. But Old Man Longjian has been hiding for the past two hundred years, hunted everywhere. Does he really have the energy to both wipe out a family and kill a noble son of a sect?"

Whether Cangshu Haoxue and the branch family died at the hands of Old Man Longjian didn't matter, because neither was important to the Cangshu family. What mattered was that their deaths provided the Cangshu family with an excuse to stir up trouble.

Dr. Hu said, "Hong Fu is also rushing to Chiyan Peak now. She has finally broken through the realm she was stuck in for two hundred years. If Chiyan Peak and Zhenyue Mountain City go to war, she would be a main force for Chiyan Peak. But her cultivation is even higher now, and I’ve gathered that she hasn't given up on finding the whereabouts of the Green-Clad Guest for the past two hundred years. If she really tracks you down, Godfather, what will you do?"

"Kill her."

Dr. Hu was left speechless for a long moment by these two decisive, cold words.

He thought to himself that Cang Shubai had tricked Hong Fu back then, causing her to develop a heart demon and affecting her cultivation. That had been somewhat unkind.

But to Cang Shubai, everyone in the world could be used. The few bottom lines and principles he held as a human were all reserved for Mu Ran.

Mu Ran bought two steaming crispy pastries. When she turned around, her expression faltered for a moment.

People were coming and going on the street, and the young man stood not far away, tall and elegant, his brows and eyes handsome, yet he seemed wrapped in an impenetrable layer of cold, radiating a distance that forbade strangers from approaching.

It wasn't until he noticed her gaze that the chill covering his face seemed to be gently brushed away by a spring breeze, melting into nothingness.

Her familiar husband was still there.

Mu Ran ran over and held the pastry to his lips. "It's still hot. Eat."

He leaned down slightly and took a bite from her hand.

She asked, "Is it good?"

Cang Shubai nodded. "It's good."

The voice in his mind returned. "Godfather, Hong Fu is a great beauty. So many cultivators want to dual-cultivate with her. If you face her, can you really bring yourself to kill such a beautiful, flower-like woman?"

"Beauty is but bones; it is merely a facade."

"But isn't Godmother also—"

Far away in a clinic in another town, Dr. Hu suddenly clutched his head and collapsed to the ground, rolling around in agony.

"Godfather, I was wrong, I was wrong! Hong Fu cannot be mentioned in the same breath as Godmother!"

Dr. Hu begged for mercy with his mouth, but in his heart, he was cursing: This scourge is just too double-standard!
